questions.stem: During a new-patient visit, a 24-year-old patient tells the physician that they were assigned female at birth and identify as a man. Which of the following terms best describes this patient's gender identity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cisgender man

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gender fluid

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intersex

choices.label: D
choices.text: Transgender man

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transgender woman

explanation.summary: A transgender man is a person assigned female at birth who identifies as a man.
explanation.whyCorrect: Transgender is the umbrella term for people whose gender identity differs from their sex assigned at birth. The lecture defines transgender men specifically as people assigned female at birth who identify as men, a binary-oriented identity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A cisgender man's gender identity aligns with a male sex assigned at birth; this patient was assigned female.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gender fluid describes an identity that is not fixed and changes over time; this patient states a consistent male identity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Intersex refers to congenital differences in chromosomal, gonadal, hormonal, or anatomic sex characteristics, not gender identity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A transgender woman is a person assigned male at birth who identifies as a woman, the reverse of this patient.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 17-year-old describes choosing clothing, a hairstyle, and speech patterns that present their gender to others in a way that feels authentic. Which of the following terms refers to this outward presentation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gender binary

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gender expression

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gender identity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sex assigned at birth

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sexual orientation

explanation.summary: Gender expression is a person's outward presentation of gender through clothing, behavior, and speech.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture defines gender expression as the outward presentation of gender, for example through clothing, behavior, and speech, and notes it may or may not align with cultural norms or with the person's gender identity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The gender binary is a classification system with two genders, men and women; it is not an individual's presentation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gender identity is a person's internal sense of their own gender, not the outward presentation of it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sex assigned at birth is a designation made from physical characteristics at birth, not a chosen presentation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sexual orientation describes sexual and emotional attraction to other people, not how gender is presented.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A newborn is found to have a congenital condition in which the gonadal and anatomic sex characteristics do not fit typical definitions of male or female. Which of the following terms describes this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gender dysphoria

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gender non-conformity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intersex

choices.label: D
choices.text: Non-binary

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transgender

explanation.summary: Intersex refers to congenital differences in chromosomal, gonadal, hormonal, or anatomic sex characteristics.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture defines intersex as a variety of congenital conditions involving differences in chromosomal, gonadal, hormonal, or anatomic sex characteristics that do not fit typical definitions of male or female. It is a matter of physical sex characteristics present at birth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gender dysphoria is significant distress associated with a desire to be a gender other than the one assigned at birth.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gender non-conformity describes behavior incompatible with cultural gender expectations, not anatomy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Non-binary is an umbrella term for gender identities outside the gender binary, not a congenital physical condition.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transgender describes a gender identity that differs from the sex assigned at birth, not congenital anatomic findings.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A family health center is redesigning its patient registration process to be more welcoming to LGBTQIA2+ patients. Which of the following changes is most consistent with recommended inclusive practice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adding an intake-form field for chosen name and pronouns

choices.label: B
choices.text: Asking patients to state their pronouns aloud in the waiting room

choices.label: C
choices.text: Having front-desk staff infer pronouns from each patient's appearance

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recording only the name printed on legal identification documents

choices.label: E
choices.text: Restricting the sex and gender fields to male or female options

explanation.summary: Intake and registration forms should let patients indicate their preferred name and pronouns, even when these differ from legal documents.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture identifies intake and registration forms as an excellent opportunity to standardize inclusive language, and notes many organizations recommend allowing patients to indicate their preferred name and pronouns, especially when they differ from legal identification and billing information.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Forms provide the recommended standardized route; requiring public verbal disclosure is not the practice the lecture describes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pronouns cannot be determined from physical appearance; they should be asked, not assumed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Limiting records to the legal name ignores patients whose preferred name differs from their identification documents.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A male-or-female-only field excludes patients; asking gender identity and the sex on the original birth certificate is preferred.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A physician is beginning a sexual history with a 19-year-old woman at a routine visit. Which of the following opening questions is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: "Are you in a relationship?"

choices.label: B
choices.text: "Do you have a boyfriend or husband?"

choices.label: C
choices.text: "How long have you been with your girlfriend?"

choices.label: D
choices.text: "How many men have you slept with this year?"

choices.label: E
choices.text: "Is your partner the same sex as you?"

explanation.summary: Open-ended questions gather history without stereotyping or assumptions about partners.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that open-ended questions allow information gathering without stereotyping or assumptions, and gives "Are you in a relationship?" as the preferred alternative. Providers should not assume the number, gender, or sex of partners or the duration of relationships.

whyWrongByChoice.B: This assumes the patient's partner would be male; the lecture lists it as a phrase to avoid.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This assumes both that a relationship exists and the partner's gender.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This assumes the gender of partners and presumes sexual activity rather than asking openly.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This assumes a partner exists; an open-ended question should establish that first.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 28-year-old transgender woman with prior distressing healthcare experiences appears anxious before a physical examination. Which of the following approaches best reduces the risk of further trauma during the encounter?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Asking a family member to remain in the room for all future visits

choices.label: B
choices.text: Completing the examination as quickly as possible without discussion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deferring all examinations until the patient no longer reports anxiety

choices.label: D
choices.text: Requiring psychiatric evaluation before any physical examination

choices.label: E
choices.text: Screening for trauma and applying trauma-informed care practices

explanation.summary: Screening for trauma and implementing trauma-informed care creates a safe environment during history taking and examination.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture advises screening for trauma and implementing trauma-informed care, especially during history taking and physical examinations, which can be particularly sensitive. Trauma-informed care training helps create a physically and emotionally safe environment that reduces the risk of further trauma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Imposing a third party is not the described approach and does not address the patient's trauma history.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Rushing through a sensitive examination without communication does not create the safe environment trauma-informed care requires.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Indefinitely deferring needed care withholds services rather than making the encounter safe.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The lecture recommends trauma-informed practices by the treating clinician, not a mandatory psychiatric gatekeeping step.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 12-year-old assigned male at birth who identifies as a girl wants more time before deciding on further gender-affirming treatment, and her family asks about "puberty blockers." Which of the following statements about GnRH analogue therapy is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It delays puberty, and puberty resumes if the medication is stopped

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is irreversible and is therefore reserved for adults

choices.label: C
choices.text: It may be started in any state without specialist supervision

choices.label: D
choices.text: It permanently prevents development of secondary sex characteristics

choices.label: E
choices.text: It produces feminizing changes such as breast development

explanation.summary: GnRH analogues reversibly delay the emergence of secondary sex characteristics; puberty resumes when therapy stops.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture describes hormone blockers as GnRH analogues that delay secondary sex characteristics such as facial hair growth, menstruation, voice changes, and breast development, giving the patient time to decide before pursuing further interventions. Puberty resumes if the therapy is stopped.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The effects are reversible, which is precisely why they are used in young adolescents who need time to decide.
whyWrongByChoice.C: They are available in some states under the supervision of a pediatric endocrinologist, not without specialist oversight everywhere.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Blockade is temporary, not permanent; puberty resumes after discontinuation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Blockers delay pubertal changes; they do not themselves feminize. Feminizing changes come from hormone therapy or surgery.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: The parents of a 10-year-old who socially transitioned one year ago worry that their child will later reverse the transition. Based on the evidence cited in the lecture, which of the following is the most accurate counseling statement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Detransition is infrequent; over 90% still identify as transgender at five years

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most youth abandon their identity once puberty blockers are stopped

choices.label: C
choices.text: Roughly half of these youth reverse their transition within five years

choices.label: D
choices.text: Social transition reliably prevents any later change in identity

choices.label: E
choices.text: There are no published data on identity after social transition

explanation.summary: Detransition after social transition is infrequent; over 90% of youth still identify as transgender five years later.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture cites Olson et al. (2022): within five years of social transitioning, over 90% of youth still identify as transgender, and detransition, the discontinuation or reversal of some aspects of a prior transition, is infrequent.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Stopping puberty blockers allows puberty to resume; it is not described as ending a transgender identity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The cited figure is the opposite: more than 90% persist in a transgender identity at five years.
whyWrongByChoice.D: No intervention guarantees a fixed identity; the accurate statement is that detransition is uncommon, not impossible.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The lecture cites a published five-year follow-up study (Olson et al., 2022, Pediatrics).

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A pediatrician counsels the family of a 15-year-old transgender boy about supporting him at home. According to survey data cited in the lecture, which of the following household practices is associated with a roughly 50% lower likelihood of a suicide attempt?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delaying any discussion of gender until age 18

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enrolling him in a single-sex school program

choices.label: C
choices.text: Limiting his contact with LGBTQIA2+ peers

choices.label: D
choices.text: Respecting the adolescent's pronouns at home

choices.label: E
choices.text: Scheduling mandatory weekly psychiatric evaluations

explanation.summary: Youth whose pronouns were respected by household members were 50% less likely to attempt suicide.
explanation.whyCorrect: The Trevor Project's 2021 survey, cited in the lecture, found that youth whose pronouns were respected by members of their household were 50% less likely to attempt suicide than youth whose pronouns were not respected. Being able to change one's name socially or legally was also associated with lower attempt rates.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Withholding affirmation is the opposite of the respected-pronoun support the data describe.
whyWrongByChoice.B: School program type is not the household practice linked to reduced suicide attempts in the cited survey.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Isolation is not protective; discrimination and negative experiences drive risk in this population.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mandated evaluations are not the protective factor identified; the cited data concern affirmation at home.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 15-year-old assigned female at birth reports persistent, significant distress related to a strong desire to be a gender other than the one assigned at birth. Which of the following statements best reflects how the DSM-5 conceptualizes gender dysphoria?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any transgender identity meets the criteria for gender dysphoria

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gender non-conforming expression alone establishes the diagnosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: The condition is classified as a disorder of sexual orientation

choices.label: D
choices.text: The diagnosis is defined by the distress, not by the gender identity itself

choices.label: E
choices.text: The diagnosis requires completion of medical transition

explanation.summary: In DSM-5, the "disorder" in gender dysphoria lies in the significant distress, not in the gender identity or expression.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that DSM-5 defines gender dysphoria as significant stress associated with a desire to be a gender other than the one assigned at birth, and emphasizes that the disorder lies in the stress rather than in the identity or expression itself. Patients with dysphoria are at higher risk for psychiatric illness and suicide.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Transgender status itself is not a disorder; only the associated significant distress defines gender dysphoria.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gender non-conformity is behavior outside cultural expectations and is not itself a diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gender identity is distinct from sexual orientation; the diagnosis concerns identity-related distress, not attraction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: No transition step is part of the definition; the diagnosis rests on distress about incongruence.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 32-year-old transgender man who has undergone mastectomy with chest reconstruction presents for a health-maintenance visit. He has not had a hysterectomy. Which of the following is most appropriate regarding cancer screening for this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Base screening decisions on gender identity rather than anatomy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continue cervical cancer screening because he has a cervix

choices.label: C
choices.text: Defer screening decisions until all planned surgeries are complete

choices.label: D
choices.text: Discontinue all cancer screening after gender-affirming surgery

choices.label: E
choices.text: Offer only the screening tests recommended for cisgender men

explanation.summary: Screening and care should continue in alignment with the patient's anatomy, regardless of gender.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that regardless of gender, screening and care in alignment with a patient's anatomy should continue, and gives exactly this example: cervical cancer screening is relevant for transgender men who have a cervix. This patient has not had a hysterectomy, so his cervix remains and screening continues.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anatomy, not gender identity, determines which organ-based screenings apply.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Screening of present anatomy should continue now, not wait on possible future procedures.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gender-affirming surgery does not remove the need for screening of organs that remain.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A cisgender-male screening panel would omit cervical cancer screening despite the retained cervix.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 26-year-old transgender woman presents with a complication of an illness for which she delayed seeking care for several months. According to survey data cited in the lecture, which of the following is the most likely reason transgender patients postpone needed care?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A legal requirement for psychiatric clearance before visits

choices.label: B
choices.text: A preference for care exclusively in emergency departments

choices.label: C
choices.text: Confidence that most symptoms resolve without treatment

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fear of discrimination in healthcare settings

choices.label: E
choices.text: Higher-than-average rates of health insurance coverage

explanation.summary: Fear of discrimination is a documented reason transgender patients postpone care; 1 in 5 did so in the past year.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture cites survey data showing 1 in 5 transgender people postponed receiving care in the past year due to fear of discrimination, and 29% reported having to teach their providers about transgender health issues. Fear of stigma and discrimination, prior uncomfortable experiences, financial concerns, and refusal of care all limit access.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No such legal clearance requirement is described; the cited barrier is fear of discrimination.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The cited data describe postponing care out of fear of discrimination, not a preference for a different care setting.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Delayed care in this population reflects barriers such as discrimination, not confidence in spontaneous recovery.
whyWrongByChoice.E: LGBTQIA2+ individuals are less likely to have health insurance and less likely to have needed services covered.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A healthy newborn is designated female in the delivery room. According to the lecture, this designation is most often based on which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chromosomal analysis of cord blood

choices.label: B
choices.text: External genitalia observed at birth

choices.label: C
choices.text: Imaging of the internal reproductive organs

choices.label: D
choices.text: The gender the parents plan to raise the child

choices.label: E
choices.text: The newborn's hormone profile

explanation.summary: Sex assignment at birth is usually based on the external genitalia observed at birth.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture defines sex assignment at birth as the designation of an infant as male or female based on physical sex characteristics observed at birth, usually the external genitalia. Chromosomes, internal reproductive organs, and hormone profiles may also contribute, but they are not the usual basis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chromosomal classification may also be included, but the usual basis is the external genitalia, not routine karyotyping.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Internal reproductive organs can contribute to classification but are not the usual basis of the delivery-room designation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sex assignment is based on physical sex characteristics, not on parental plans; gender identity is a separate concept that emerges from the person.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hormone profiles may be included in some classifications, but they are not the usual basis at birth.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 7-year-old assigned male at birth consistently says he is a boy but prefers clothing and play activities that his community considers typical for girls. Which of the following terms best describes this child's behavior?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gender dysphoria

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gender non-conformity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gender-normative behavior

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intersex condition

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transgender identity

explanation.summary: Behavior incompatible with cultural gender expectations is gender non-conformity.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that behavior compatible with cultural expectations is gender-normative, while behaviors incompatible with these expectations may be described as gender non-conformity. This child's stated identity matches his sex assigned at birth; only his behavior departs from cultural expectations, and different cultures can have different expectations for specific genders.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gender dysphoria requires significant distress about a desire to be a gender other than the one assigned at birth; no distress or such desire is described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gender-normative describes behavior compatible with cultural expectations, the opposite of this child's preferences.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Intersex refers to congenital differences in chromosomal, gonadal, hormonal, or anatomic sex characteristics, not to behavior.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transgender describes a gender identity that differs from the sex assigned at birth; this child identifies as a boy.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman tells her physician that she experiences romantic and sexual attraction exclusively to other women. Which of the following concepts does this description represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gender binary

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gender expression

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gender identity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sex assigned at birth

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sexual orientation

explanation.summary: Sexual orientation is a person's sexual and emotional attraction to other people.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture defines sexual orientation as a person's sexual and emotional attraction to other people, along with the behavior or social affiliation that may result. A person may be attracted to men, women, neither, or people of other gender identities. Attraction is a separate dimension from a person's own gender.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The gender binary is a classification system with two genders; it does not describe attraction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gender expression is the outward presentation of gender through clothing, behavior, and speech.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gender identity is a person's internal sense of their own gender, not whom they are attracted to.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sex assigned at birth is the designation made from physical characteristics at birth, not a pattern of attraction.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A clinic's old intake form requires every patient to register as either a man or a woman, with no other options. This form's design reflects which of the following classification systems?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cisgender identity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gender binary

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gender expression

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gender-normative behavior

choices.label: E
choices.text: Non-binary classification

explanation.summary: The gender binary is a system whereby all individuals are classified as one of two possible genders, men and women.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture defines the gender binary as a system in which everyone is classified as a man or a woman. Cisgender men, cisgender women, transgender men, and transgender women are all examples of binary-oriented identities, but a two-option form excludes the non-binary umbrella of genders outside that system.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cisgender describes a person whose identity and expression align with their sex assigned at birth; it is an identity, not a classification system.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gender expression is an individual's outward presentation of gender, not a system for classifying people.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gender-normative describes behavior compatible with cultural expectations, not a classification scheme on a form.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Non-binary is an umbrella term for genders that are not part of a gender binary; a two-option form is the opposite of this.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 20-year-old patient explains that their sense of their own gender is not fixed: during some periods they experience themselves as a man, and during others as neither a man nor a woman. Which of the following terms specifically describes a gender identity that changes over time?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cisgender

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gender fluid

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intersex

choices.label: D
choices.text: Questioning

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transgender man

explanation.summary: Gender fluid describes a person whose gender identity is not fixed and can change over time.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture defines gender fluid as a gender identity that is not fixed and can change over time, which matches this patient's description of shifting between identifying as a man and as neither a man nor a woman.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cisgender describes identity and expression that align with the sex assigned at birth and remain a single stable gender.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Intersex refers to congenital differences in physical sex characteristics, not to gender identity over time.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Questioning refers to exploring one's identity, not to an identity that is itself defined by changing over time.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A transgender man is a person assigned female at birth who identifies as a man; this patient describes a changing identity, not a fixed male one.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: During intake, a patient from a First Nations community tells the physician that they identify as Two-Spirit. Which of the following is the most accurate understanding of this term?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A congenital difference in sex characteristics

choices.label: B
choices.text: A culturally specific identity used by some Indigenous people

choices.label: C
choices.text: A gender identity that alternates between two fixed states

choices.label: D
choices.text: A stage of actively exploring one's own identity

choices.label: E
choices.text: A synonym for bisexual attraction to two genders

explanation.summary: Two-Spirit, the "2" in LGBTQIA2+, is a culturally specific identity used by some Indigenous/First Nations people.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture defines Two-Spirit as a culturally specific identity used by some Indigenous/First Nations people; it is represented by the "2" in the LGBTQIA2+ acronym. Understanding this cultural specificity supports respectful, patient-centered communication.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Congenital differences in chromosomal, gonadal, hormonal, or anatomic sex characteristics define intersex, not Two-Spirit.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An identity that changes over time is described as gender fluid; Two-Spirit is not defined as alternating states.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Exploring one's identity is the meaning of questioning, a different component of the acronym.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bisexual is a separate identity within the acronym; Two-Spirit is not defined as a pattern of attraction to two genders.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 16-year-old tells their physician, "I'm still questioning." Within the LGBTQIA2+ acronym described in the lecture, which of the following does this term mean?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Experiencing no sexual attraction to others

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exploring one's own identity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Having a gender identity that differs from birth-assigned sex

choices.label: D
choices.text: Having congenital differences in sex characteristics

choices.label: E
choices.text: Presenting gender outwardly through clothing and speech

explanation.summary: Questioning, one meaning of the Q in LGBTQIA2+, means exploring one's identity.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the LGBTQIA2+ acronym, Q stands for Queer or Questioning, and the lecture defines questioning as exploring one's identity. The physician should support this exploration without assuming a fixed label.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Absence of sexual attraction describes asexual, the A in the acronym.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A gender identity differing from the sex assigned at birth describes transgender, the T in the acronym.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Congenital differences in sex characteristics define intersex, the I in the acronym.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Outward presentation of gender is gender expression, which is not what questioning means.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 25-year-old patient self-describes as queer. Based on the lecture, which of the following is the most accurate understanding of this term?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A DSM-5 psychiatric diagnosis for distress about one's gender identity

choices.label: B
choices.text: A slur that patients never use to describe themselves in the present day

choices.label: C
choices.text: A term covering gender identity only, with no reference to sexual orientation

choices.label: D
choices.text: A term that refers exclusively to gay men and to no other group in the acronym

choices.label: E
choices.text: An umbrella term covering non-conforming sexual orientation or gender identity

explanation.summary: Queer is an umbrella term for people whose sexual orientation or gender identity does not conform to heterosexual or cisgender norms.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture defines queer as an umbrella term for people whose sexual orientation or gender identity does not conform to heterosexual or cisgender norms, and notes the LGBTQIA2+ community has gradually reclaimed it as a term of empowerment and inclusivity since the 1980s. Physicians should use each patient's stated identity language.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The DSM-5 diagnosis related to identity distress is gender dysphoria; queer is an identity term, not a diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The community has reclaimed queer as a term of empowerment since the 1980s, and this patient is using it for self-description.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The term covers both dimensions: sexual orientation that is not heterosexual and gender identity that is not cisgender.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Queer spans many orientations and gender identities; gay is a separate, narrower term within the acronym.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A child arrives at a family health center accompanied by an adult. Following the lecture's inclusive-terminology guidance, which of the following is the best way for staff to ask about their relationship?

choices.label: A
choices.text: "Is this your dad or your stepdad?"

choices.label: B
choices.text: "Is this your mother?"

choices.label: C
choices.text: "Is this your parent?"

choices.label: D
choices.text: "Is your mom parking the car?"

choices.label: E
choices.text: "Where is your father today?"

explanation.summary: Neutral terms such as "parent" or "guardian" show welcome without assuming family structure.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture gives this exact example of inclusive terminology: use "is this your parent?" instead of "is this your mother?" Its terminology table likewise replaces "Mother or Father" with "Parents or Guardians," avoiding assumptions about who cares for the child.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This assumes the adult is male and restricts the relationship to two specific roles.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is the lecture's example of the phrasing to avoid, since it assumes the adult's role and gender.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This assumes a mother exists and is nearby rather than asking neutrally about the accompanying adult.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This assumes the child has a father involved in their care and implies he should be present.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A physician reviews a colleague's clinic note that describes a patient as "transexual." According to the lecture's inclusive-terminology table, which of the following terms should be used instead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gender fluid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intersex

choices.label: C
choices.text: Queer

choices.label: D
choices.text: Transgender

choices.label: E
choices.text: Two-Spirit

explanation.summary: The inclusive-terminology table lists "transexual" as a term to avoid, with "transgender" as the suggested alternative.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture's table of terms to avoid versus suggested alternatives pairs "transexual" directly with "transgender." Transgender is the umbrella term for individuals whose gender identity differs from their sex assigned at birth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gender fluid describes an identity that changes over time and is not the suggested substitute.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Intersex refers to congenital differences in sex characteristics, a different concept entirely.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Queer is a broader umbrella term for non-conforming orientation or identity; it is not the table's replacement for this word.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Two-Spirit is a culturally specific Indigenous identity, not a general replacement term.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A physician is taking a sexual history from a 30-year-old man presenting for a routine visit. Which of the following practices is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask detailed questions about every past relationship regardless of relevance

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assume his sexual relationships have been long-term

choices.label: C
choices.text: Confine questions to those relevant to his care

choices.label: D
choices.text: Discuss partners only if the patient raises the topic first

choices.label: E
choices.text: Infer the gender of his partners from his appearance

explanation.summary: History questions should be open-ended, free of assumptions, and confined to what is relevant to the patient's care.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture instructs providers not to assume the number of partners, the gender or sex of partners, or the duration of sexual relationships, and to confine questions to those relevant to the patient's care. Open-ended questions gather information without stereotyping.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Exhaustive questioning beyond what care requires is the opposite of confining questions to relevant ones.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Providers should not assume the duration of sexual relationships.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A sexual history relevant to care should still be taken with open-ended questions, not omitted until the patient volunteers it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gender of partners cannot be assumed, and pronouns and identities cannot be determined from appearance.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: The care team of a 13-year-old transgender girl consistently uses her chosen name and pronouns in all interactions. Within the framework of gender-affirming care described in the lecture, this practice is best classified as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A legal change

choices.label: B
choices.text: A medical intervention

choices.label: C
choices.text: A psychological counseling service

choices.label: D
choices.text: A social intervention

choices.label: E
choices.text: A surgical intervention

explanation.summary: Use of a person's chosen name and pronouns is a social intervention within gender-affirming care.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture describes gender-affirming care as a range of interventions that reduce distress from incongruence between gender identity and sex assigned at birth, and it lists the use of a person's chosen name and pronouns specifically under social interventions, alongside psychological support, medical interventions such as hormone therapy, and surgical interventions in selected patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Legal changes involve identity documents; using a chosen name in conversation does not require any legal step.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Medical interventions are clinically indicated treatments such as hormone therapy, not naming practices.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Psychological support and counseling are a separate category from the everyday social practice of using chosen names and pronouns.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Surgical interventions are procedures offered to selected patients, not communication practices.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: The parents of an 8-year-old assigned female at birth who identifies as a boy ask what steps are available for a child his age. According to the lecture, which of the following is an option for children?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Beginning masculinizing hormone therapy immediately at this visit

choices.label: B
choices.text: Choosing a hairstyle, clothing, and pronouns that express his gender

choices.label: C
choices.text: Completing voice masculinization surgical procedures

choices.label: D
choices.text: Scheduling metoidioplasty with the surgical team

choices.label: E
choices.text: Undergoing mastectomy with chest wall reconstruction surgery

explanation.summary: Children can transition socially through gender expression, name, pronouns, and, in some states, bathroom use.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that children can transition socially by choosing how to express their gender through clothing, changing their hairstyle, legally changing their name, using gender-affirming pronouns, and, in some states, using bathrooms that match their gender identity. Options for minors depend on age, parental consent, and federal and state laws.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hormone therapy is a medical intervention; the option the lecture describes for children is social transition.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Voice masculinization is a surgical option, not part of a child's social transition.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Metoidioplasty is a masculinizing surgical procedure, not an option described for a young child.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Masculinizing top surgery is a surgical intervention; in some states surgery is available only to older adolescents, roughly 16-19 years of age.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 16-year-old requests gender-affirming medical treatment. In exploring whether medical intervention is right for this patient, which of the following questions does the lecture recommend?

choices.label: A
choices.text: "Are you sure this is not just a phase?"

choices.label: B
choices.text: "What are some of your goals and expectations?"

choices.label: C
choices.text: "Which procedures do your friends recommend?"

choices.label: D
choices.text: "Why not wait until you are 18 to decide?"

choices.label: E
choices.text: "Wouldn't social transition be enough at your age?"

explanation.summary: Exploring goals and expectations is one of the lecture's recommended questions before medical or surgical intervention.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture lists questions to explore when considering medical or surgical intervention: how long the patient has felt this way, how it has impacted daily life, why they want to transition, their goals and expectations, and their past and planned gender-affirming care.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dismissing the identity as a phase is not among the recommended questions and undermines respectful, patient-centered communication.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Care decisions rest on the patient's own goals and clinical indication, not on peers' preferences.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Options for minors depend on age, parental consent, and applicable laws; deflecting until adulthood is not one of the lecture's exploration questions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Steering the patient toward a predetermined option substitutes the physician's assumption for the patient's stated goals.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A physician counsels a family using data from the Trevor Project's 2021 National Survey on LGBTQ Youth Mental Health. Approximately what proportion of transgender and nonbinary youth reported seriously considering suicide in the past year?

explanation.summary: In the 2021 Trevor Project survey, 52% of transgender and nonbinary youth seriously considered suicide in the past year.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture cites the Trevor Project's 2021 National Survey on LGBTQ Youth Mental Health: 52% of transgender and nonbinary youth had seriously considered suicide in the past year, and 20% had attempted suicide in the past year. These data underscore why affirming environments matter.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 5% far understates the reported burden of suicidal ideation in this population.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 20% is the survey's figure for suicide attempts in the past year, not for serious consideration of suicide.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 75% is not the cited figure; the survey reported 52% for serious consideration.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 90% is close to the proportion of youth who still identify as transgender five years after social transition, a different statistic.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 12-year-old in early puberty is starting a GnRH analogue for gender-affirming care in a state where this is available. According to the lecture, this therapy is provided under the supervision of which of the following specialists?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Child and adolescent psychiatrist

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clinical medical geneticist

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pediatric endocrinologist

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pediatric urologic surgeon

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reproductive tract surgeon

explanation.summary: Puberty blockers are available in some states under the supervision of a pediatric endocrinologist.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that hormone blockers, or puberty blockers (GnRH analogues), are available in some states under the supervision of a pediatric endocrinologist. They delay the emergence of secondary sex characteristics such as facial hair growth, menstruation, voice changes, and breast development.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Psychiatric and psychological support is part of gender-affirming care, but hormone blockade is supervised by pediatric endocrinology.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Genetics is not involved in supervising GnRH analogue therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Urology is not the specialty the lecture assigns to puberty-blocker management.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Surgeons perform gender-affirming procedures; they are not the specialists the lecture names for puberty-blocker supervision.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 30-year-old transgender woman is planning gender-affirming genital surgery. Which of the following is a feminizing surgical procedure described in the lecture?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hysterectomy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Metoidioplasty

choices.label: C
choices.text: Phalloplasty

choices.label: D
choices.text: Scrotoplasty

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vaginoplasty

explanation.summary: Vaginoplasty is a feminizing surgical procedure; the other options listed are masculinizing procedures.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture lists vaginoplasty among feminizing surgical procedures, together with top surgery (breast augmentation), orchiectomy, facial feminization, and voice feminization, which consists of multiple procedures.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hysterectomy, with or without salpingo-oophorectomy, is listed under masculinizing procedures.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Metoidioplasty is listed among the masculinizing surgical procedures.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Phalloplasty is a masculinizing genital procedure, the opposite direction from this patient's goals.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Scrotoplasty is a masculinizing procedure.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 24-year-old transgender man asks his physician about "top surgery." For masculinizing purposes, this term refers to which of the following procedures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Breast augmentation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Facial masculinization

choices.label: C
choices.text: Masculinizing body contouring by liposuction

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mastectomy with chest reconstruction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Voice masculinization

explanation.summary: Masculinizing top surgery is mastectomy with chest reconstruction; feminizing top surgery is breast augmentation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture uses "top surgery" for both directions but with opposite meanings: in the masculinizing list it is mastectomy with chest reconstruction, whereas in the feminizing list it is breast augmentation. For a transgender man, top surgery means the former.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Breast augmentation is top surgery in the feminizing direction, not the masculinizing one.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Facial masculinization is a separate masculinizing procedure, not what top surgery denotes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Body contouring, such as liposuction to create a traditionally masculine torso, is listed separately from top surgery.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Voice masculinization is its own procedure and does not involve the chest.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 17-year-old transgender woman asks whether gender-affirming surgery could be an option before she turns 18. Based on the lecture, which of the following is the most accurate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Federal law guarantees surgical access at 16 years nationwide

choices.label: B
choices.text: In some states, surgical interventions are available to older adolescents

choices.label: C
choices.text: Surgery is offered at any age once parental consent is obtained

choices.label: D
choices.text: Surgery is permitted only after puberty blockers prove ineffective

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surgery is prohibited in every state before 21 years of age

explanation.summary: In some states, gender-affirming surgical interventions are available to older adolescents, roughly 16-19 years of age.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that feminizing and masculinizing surgeries can change physical characteristics and that, in some states, gender-affirming surgical interventions are available to older adolescents (approximately 16-19 years of age). Options for minors depend on age, parental consent, and federal and state laws.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Access is state-dependent; the lecture describes no federal guarantee at any age.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Age and state law matter alongside parental consent; the lecture describes availability for older adolescents, not children of any age.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Puberty blockers buy time for decision-making; the lecture describes no requirement that they fail before surgery is considered.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Availability varies by state, and some states permit surgery for older adolescents; no universal age-21 prohibition is described.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A medical student asks why LGBTQIA2+ patients have higher rates of depression and anxiety. According to the lecture, which of the following is the most accurate explanation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gender-affirming hormone therapy commonly triggers depression

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intersex conditions inherently impair mental health

choices.label: C
choices.text: Negative experiences and discrimination increase vulnerability

choices.label: D
choices.text: Same-sex attraction is itself a risk factor for mental illness

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transgender identity directly causes mood disorders

explanation.summary: Identity itself is not a risk factor; negative experiences and discrimination drive the elevated mental health burden.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that same-sex attraction, transgender status, and intersex conditions are not themselves risk factors for mental health problems, but they may make people more vulnerable to negative experiences and discrimination, two factors that affect both mental and physical health.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gender-affirming interventions are associated with improved mental health outcomes in the cited observational studies, not with causing depression.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Intersex conditions are listed with the other identities that are not themselves risk factors.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The lecture explicitly says same-sex attraction is not itself a risk factor for mental health problems.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transgender status is not itself pathogenic; even in gender dysphoria, the disorder lies in the distress, not the identity.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: According to the Trevor Project National Survey (2022) cited in the lecture, queer youth are how many times more likely than their cisgender heterosexual peers to experience mood disorders and substance abuse?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 1.5 times

choices.label: B
choices.text: 2.5 times

choices.label: C
choices.text: 4 times

choices.label: D
choices.text: 6 times

choices.label: E
choices.text: 10 times

explanation.summary: Queer youth are 2.5 times more likely to experience mood disorders and substance abuse than cisgender heterosexual peers.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture cites the Trevor Project National Survey (2022) finding that queer youth are 2.5 times more likely to experience mood disorders and substance abuse compared with their cisgender heterosexual peers, part of the population's higher rates of depression, anxiety, and suicide.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 1.5 times understates the cited disparity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 4 times overstates the cited figure of 2.5.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 6 times is not the survey figure the lecture reports.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 10 times greatly overstates the cited relative likelihood.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 15-year-old with gender dysphoria begins psychotherapy. According to the lecture, which of the following is a goal of psychotherapy in this setting?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Certifying eligibility for surgical intervention

choices.label: B
choices.text: Confirming that the identity will never change

choices.label: C
choices.text: Developing skills to cope with non-affirming spaces

choices.label: D
choices.text: Redirecting gender identity toward the sex assigned at birth

choices.label: E
choices.text: Replacing the need for any social transition

explanation.summary: Psychotherapy helps youths cope with the impacts of dysphoria and stigma, boost body positivity, and build resilience.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that psychotherapy for youths helps address the negative impact of gender dysphoria and stigma on mental health, develops skills to cope with the negative impacts of non-affirming spaces, boosts body positivity, and promotes overall resilience.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The lecture describes therapy as supportive treatment, not a gatekeeping certification for surgery.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Therapy builds coping and resilience; it does not exist to declare an identity permanent.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The disorder in gender dysphoria lies in the distress, not the identity; therapy targets distress and coping, not changing the identity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Social interventions remain a distinct component of gender-affirming care; therapy does not substitute for them.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A physician notes that a young transgender patient's health is being shaped by household poverty, homelessness, and unemployment. According to the World Health Organization (2021) definition cited in the lecture, these are best described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diagnostic criteria for gender dysphoria

choices.label: B
choices.text: Genetic determinants of disease susceptibility

choices.label: C
choices.text: Iatrogenic complications of medical care

choices.label: D
choices.text: Non-medical factors that influence health outcomes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Voluntary lifestyle choices unrelated to health access

explanation.summary: Social determinants of health are non-medical factors that influence health outcomes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture cites the WHO (2021) definition of social determinants of health as non-medical factors that influence health outcomes; they affect daily life and ultimately access to and quality of health care. Household poverty, homelessness, incarceration, unemployment, and lack of post-secondary education disproportionately affect LGBTQIA2+ individuals.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gender dysphoria is defined by distress about gender incongruence; social hardship is not among its defining criteria.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Social determinants are environmental and societal, not genetic, factors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: These circumstances arise outside the healthcare system rather than being caused by medical care.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Poverty, homelessness, and unemployment are structural circumstances, and they directly affect access to and quality of care.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A transgender patient mentions spending much of a recent appointment explaining transgender health basics to the clinician. According to survey data cited in the lecture, approximately what proportion of transgender people report having had to teach their providers about transgender health issues?

explanation.summary: 29% of transgender people reported having to teach their providers about transgender health issues.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture cites the Trevor Project National Survey (2022): 29% of transgender people reported having to teach their providers about transgender health issues. Access is limited by the need to find providers willing and knowledgeable to provide care, and 1 in 5 transgender people postponed care in the past year due to fear of discrimination.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 3% greatly understates the cited proportion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 9% is well below the reported figure of 29%.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 59% overstates the cited figure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 89% is far above the proportion the survey reported.

questions.topicName: Inclusive Language and Health Equity

questions.stem: A 16-year-old with a female phenotype is evaluated for primary amenorrhea and delayed puberty. Karyotype analysis reveals 46,XY, and pelvic imaging shows a uterus and bilateral streak gonads. Which of the following best explains this presentation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Excess maternal androgen exposure during gestation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Failure of the indifferent gonads to develop into testes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Failure of the paramesonephric ducts to develop

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inability of target tissues to convert testosterone to DHT

choices.label: E
choices.text: Isolated deficiency of anti-Müllerian hormone

explanation.summary: Complete gonadal dysgenesis (46,XY Swyer) produces nonfunctional streak gonads, so no AMH or testosterone is made and a female phenotype with delayed puberty results.
explanation.whyCorrect: In complete gonadal dysgenesis, the gonads fail to develop into testes despite the Y chromosome. Streak gonads make neither AMH nor testosterone, so the Müllerian ducts persist (uterus present), the Wolffian ducts regress, and external genitalia develop along the female pathway. Absent sex hormone production also explains the delayed puberty.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Androgen excess virilizes XX fetuses; it does not produce streak gonads or a female phenotype in an XY fetus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The Müllerian ducts clearly developed, because a uterus is present on imaging.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Impaired conversion to DHT leaves functioning testes that still make AMH, so the uterus would be absent and testes would be present.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Isolated AMH deficiency (persistent Müllerian duct syndrome) produces a phenotypic male with a uterus, not a female phenotype with streak gonads.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: Beginning around week 7 of development, an XY embryo initiates testis formation. The protein that directs the indifferent gonad to differentiate into a testis is encoded by which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A gene expressed by Leydig cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: A gene expressed by Sertoli cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Genes of the urogenital sinus endoderm

choices.label: D
choices.text: Genes on the two X chromosomes

choices.label: E
choices.text: The SRY gene on the Y chromosome

explanation.summary: The SRY gene on the Y chromosome encodes testis-determining factor (TDF), which converts the indifferent gonad into a testis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The SRY (sex-determining region of the Y chromosome) gene produces testis-determining factor, also called SRY protein. TDF directs the indifferent gonad to develop into a testis with seminiferous tubules containing Sertoli cells and an interstitium containing Leydig cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Leydig cells arise after TDF acts and secrete testosterone; they do not direct gonadal differentiation into a testis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sertoli cells are a product of testis formation and secrete AMH; they do not encode the factor that initiates testis formation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Urogenital sinus endoderm gives rise to the prostate and urethra, not to the signal for testis formation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Genes on the XX chromosomes contribute to ovarian development, not testis determination.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A 2-year-old boy undergoes surgery for bilateral cryptorchidism. Intraoperatively, the surgeon finds a uterus and uterine tubes alongside otherwise normal male internal reproductive organs. A defect in which of the following best explains these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anti-Müllerian hormone or its receptor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estrogen signaling in the fetal gonad

choices.label: D
choices.text: Testosterone production by Leydig cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: The SRY gene and testis-determining factor

explanation.summary: Persistent Müllerian duct syndrome results from abnormal AMH or AMH receptors, so the paramesonephric ducts fail to regress in a male.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sertoli cells normally secrete AMH, which causes regression of the paramesonephric (Müllerian) ducts. When AMH or its receptor is abnormal, a male develops normal reproductive organs and external genitalia but also retains a uterus and uterine tubes. PMDS is often found incidentally during surgery for cryptorchidism or inguinal hernia, both characteristic of the condition.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Impaired DHT production causes undervirilized external genitalia but does not cause Müllerian structures to persist.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Estrogen from fetal ovaries supports female external development; it plays no role in Müllerian regression in males.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Testosterone must be present, because the mesonephric-duct derivatives and male external genitalia developed normally.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Without SRY and TDF, testes would not form at all; this boy has testes, although undescended.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: During an anatomy review of the male internal reproductive organs, a student is asked which structure does NOT arise from the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct. Which of the following is the correct response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ductus deferens

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ejaculatory duct

choices.label: C
choices.text: Epididymis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prostate

choices.label: E
choices.text: Seminal vesicle

explanation.summary: The mesonephric duct forms the SEED structures (seminal vesicles, epididymis, ejaculatory duct, ductus deferens); the prostate and urethra arise from the urogenital sinus.
explanation.whyCorrect: The prostate does not derive from the mesonephric duct. It arises from the endoderm of the urogenital sinus, which forms when the embryonic cloaca divides into separate urogenital and anorectal passages. The male urethra shares this urogenital sinus origin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The ductus deferens is a mesonephric-duct derivative (the D in SEED).
whyWrongByChoice.B: The ejaculatory ducts are mesonephric-duct derivatives (the second E in SEED).
whyWrongByChoice.C: The epididymis is a mesonephric-duct derivative (the E in SEED).
whyWrongByChoice.E: The seminal vesicles are mesonephric-duct derivatives (the S in SEED).

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A 16-year-old girl is evaluated because she has never menstruated. She has normal breast development and pubic hair. Examination shows a short, blind-ended vagina, and pelvic imaging shows an absent uterus with normal-appearing ovaries. Failure of which of the following structures to develop best explains her condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gonadal ridge

choices.label: B
choices.text: Labioscrotal swellings

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mesonephric ducts

choices.label: D
choices.text: Paramesonephric ducts

choices.label: E
choices.text: Urogenital sinus

explanation.summary: Müllerian agenesis (MRKH syndrome) is failure of the paramesonephric ducts to develop, so the uterus and upper vagina do not form despite normal ovaries.
explanation.whyCorrect: The paramesonephric (Müllerian) ducts normally form the uterine tubes, uterus, and upper vagina. In MRKH syndrome these ducts fail to develop, so those structures are absent. The ovaries develop from the gonad, not the ducts, so they function normally, producing normal breast and pubic hair development; the disorder is typically diagnosed when menstruation has not begun by age 16.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The gonadal ridge developed normally, since the ovaries are present and functioning.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The labioscrotal swellings form the labia majora, an external structure that is unaffected here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The mesonephric ducts normally regress in females and form male internal structures; their absence would not affect the uterus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The urogenital sinus forms the lower vagina, which is present as the short, blind-ended canal in this patient.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: In a female embryo, the caudal portions of the paramesonephric ducts fuse at the midline to form the uterus and upper vagina. The lower (caudal) portion of the vagina develops from which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Genital tubercle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mesonephric ducts

choices.label: C
choices.text: Unfused cranial paramesonephric ducts

choices.label: D
choices.text: Urogenital folds

choices.label: E
choices.text: Urogenital sinus

explanation.summary: The vagina has a dual origin: the upper vagina comes from the fused paramesonephric ducts and the lower vagina from the urogenital sinus.
explanation.whyCorrect: The caudal vagina develops from the urogenital sinus, which derives from the ventral division of the cloaca. Only the upper vagina arises from the fused caudal paramesonephric ducts.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The genital tubercle forms the glans clitoris and part of the clitoral body.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The mesonephric ducts regress in females without testosterone; they do not form the vagina.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The unfused cranial portions of the paramesonephric ducts remain as the uterine tubes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The urogenital folds form the labia minora and the openings of the urethra and vagina, not the vaginal canal itself.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: As the caudal portions of the paramesonephric ducts fuse during female development, a temporary midline uterovaginal septum forms from the walls of the fused ducts. Which of the following describes the normal fate of this septum?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It differentiates into the wall of the uterine tubes

choices.label: B
choices.text: It migrates caudally to form the lower vagina

choices.label: C
choices.text: It persists, dividing the uterus into two cavities

choices.label: D
choices.text: It regresses, producing a single continuous lumen

choices.label: E
choices.text: It thickens to become the round ligament of the uterus

explanation.summary: The transient uterovaginal septum normally regresses, leaving one continuous lumen through the uterus, cervix, and cranial vagina.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fusion of the caudal paramesonephric ducts creates the single midline uterus, cervix, and cranial vagina, and the septum formed by the fused duct walls later regresses. This regression produces a single continuous lumen in the uterus, cervix, and cranial vagina.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The uterine tubes are the unfused cranial portions of the paramesonephric ducts; they do not form from the septum.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The lower vagina forms from the urogenital sinus, not from the septum.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Persistence of the septum is not the normal outcome; regression yields one cavity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The round ligament of the uterus derives from the gubernaculum, not from the uterovaginal septum.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman gives birth to an infant with trisomy 21. Which of the following best explains why the risk of this outcome increases with advancing maternal age?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Germ cells stay quiescent until puberty and then resume mitosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: New oocytes made after birth accumulate replication errors

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oocytes arrest in metaphase II from fetal life until menopause

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ovarian follicles arrest earlier in meiosis with advancing age

choices.label: E
choices.text: Primary oocytes remain arrested in prophase I for decades

explanation.summary: Because no new oocytes are made after birth, primary oocytes stay arrested in prophase I for decades, and prolonged arrest increases the risk of nondisjunction and aneuploidy.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the fetal ovary, germ cells proliferate, begin meiosis, and arrest in prophase I as primary oocytes; the pool is fixed at birth. With advancing maternal age these long-arrested cells are more prone to meiotic errors, especially nondisjunction, raising the risk of chromosomal disorders such as Down syndrome (about 1 in 1,500 at age 18 versus about 1 in 26 at age 49).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Quiescence until puberty followed by resumed mitosis describes male germ cells, not oocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: No new oocytes are produced after birth; the pool of primary oocytes is fixed.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fetal-life arrest occurs in prophase I of meiosis I, not metaphase II.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The arrest point does not shift with age; the problem is prolonged arrest leading to nondisjunction.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: During female development, the gubernaculum extends from the developing ovary to the labioscrotal swelling. As the uterus forms, this cord is divided. In the adult, the gubernaculum is represented by which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ovarian ligament and round ligament of the uterus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Processus vaginalis and tunica vaginalis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Suspensory ligament of the ovary and broad ligament

choices.label: D
choices.text: Uterine tubes and the upper portion of the uterus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uterosacral ligament and cardinal ligament

explanation.summary: The female gubernaculum is divided by the developing uterus into the ovarian ligament and the round ligament of the uterus.
explanation.whyCorrect: As the uterus develops, the gubernaculum is divided into the ovarian ligament, connecting the ovary to the uterus, and the round ligament of the uterus, which runs from the uterus through the inguinal canal to the labia majora. The ovaries themselves undergo only limited caudal migration into the pelvis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The processus vaginalis is a peritoneal pouch that accompanies the descending testis; its distal portion becomes the tunica vaginalis in males.
whyWrongByChoice.C: These ligaments are not derived from the gubernaculum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The uterine tubes and uterus arise from the paramesonephric ducts, not from the gubernaculum.
whyWrongByChoice.E: These pelvic support ligaments are not gubernacular derivatives.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: Beginning around week 26, the testis is guided through the inguinal canal into the scrotum, accompanied by a small pouch of peritoneum. The distal portion of this peritoneal pouch normally becomes which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dartos layer of the scrotum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Duct of the seminal vesicle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ductus deferens (vas deferens)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gubernaculum of the testis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tunica vaginalis of the testis

explanation.summary: The processus vaginalis accompanies the descending testis; its distal portion becomes the tunica vaginalis while its proximal connection to the abdomen normally closes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The processus vaginalis is the pouch of peritoneum that travels with the testis during descent. Its distal portion persists as the tunica vaginalis of the testis, and the proximal connection to the abdominal cavity normally closes after descent is complete.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The scrotum develops from the labioscrotal swellings of the external genitalia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The seminal vesicles arise from the mesonephric ducts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The ductus deferens is a mesonephric-duct derivative, not a peritoneal structure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The gubernaculum is the fibrous cord that guides the descent and then regresses; it is not derived from peritoneum.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A newborn with a 46,XX karyotype was exposed to excess androgens in utero and is noted to have fusion of the labioscrotal swellings. In a male fetus, these same swellings normally give rise to which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bulbourethral glands

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glans penis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Penile urethra

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prostate

choices.label: E
choices.text: Scrotum

explanation.summary: The labioscrotal swellings form the scrotum in males and the labia majora in females, making these structures embryologic homologs.
explanation.whyCorrect: The three shared precursors of the external genitalia differentiate beginning around week 9. The labioscrotal swellings become the scrotum in males and the labia majora in females. Androgen excess in an XX fetus virilizes the external genitalia, producing labial fusion, while internal female organs remain normal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The bulbourethral glands arise from the urogenital sinus, homologous to the greater vestibular glands.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The glans penis derives from the genital tubercle, whose female homolog is the glans clitoris.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The penile urethra forms when the urogenital folds fuse along the ventral midline of the developing penis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The prostate arises from the urogenital sinus, homologous to the female urethral and paraurethral glands.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A newborn with a 46,XY karyotype has poorly virilized external genitalia. Evaluation shows testes, a normal epididymis and ductus deferens bilaterally, and no uterus or uterine tubes. Serum testosterone is within the normal male range. A deficiency of which of the following best explains the external genital findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anti-Müllerian hormone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dihydrotestosterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estrogen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Testis-determining factor

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testosterone

explanation.summary: Male external genitalia require DHT, a tissue-derived product of testosterone; without DHT the external genitalia follow the female pathway even when internal male ducts are intact.
explanation.whyCorrect: Differentiation of the external genitalia in males is driven by dihydrotestosterone, made in target tissues from testosterone. Testosterone alone maintained the mesonephric-duct derivatives (epididymis, ductus deferens), and AMH caused Müllerian regression, but without adequate DHT the genital tubercle, urogenital folds, and labioscrotal swellings fail to fully virilize.

whyWrongByChoice.A: AMH acted normally, because the uterus and uterine tubes are absent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Estrogen from fetal ovaries supports female external development; its absence does not impair male virilization.
whyWrongByChoice.D: TDF functioned, since testes formed from the indifferent gonads.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serum testosterone is normal, and its duct derivatives (epididymis, ductus deferens) developed appropriately.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A transverse section of a 5-week embryo shows the indifferent gonads and both paired duct systems arising on the posterior abdominal wall. These structures are derived from which of the following embryonic tissues?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Endoderm of the cloaca

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intermediate mesoderm

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lateral plate mesoderm

choices.label: D
choices.text: Paraxial mesoderm

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surface ectoderm

explanation.summary: During the indifferent stage (roughly weeks 4-6), the gonads and both duct systems arise from intermediate mesoderm on the posterior abdominal wall.
explanation.whyCorrect: The foundational reproductive structures of the indifferent stage all come from the intermediate mesoderm. A thickening of intermediate mesoderm becomes the gonadal ridge by week 5, and the mesonephric (Wolffian) and paramesonephric (Müllerian) ducts develop alongside it on the posterior abdominal wall.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cloacal derivatives such as the urogenital sinus contribute the prostate, urethra, and lower vagina, not the gonads or the paired ducts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lateral plate mesoderm is not the source of the gonadal ridge or duct systems.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Paraxial mesoderm is not the source of the gonads or reproductive ducts.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Surface ectoderm does not give rise to the indifferent gonads or ducts.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: In a 6-week embryo, the mesonephric (Wolffian) ducts are already active before any reproductive differentiation has occurred. At this stage, these ducts serve which of the following roles?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Forming the endodermal lining of the urogenital sinus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Functioning as part of the embryonic kidney

choices.label: C
choices.text: Producing anti-Müllerian hormone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Secreting testosterone to support the indifferent gonad

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transporting primordial germ cells into the gonadal ridge

explanation.summary: The mesonephric ducts initially function as part of the embryonic kidney (the mesonephros); they persist after the mesonephros regresses.
explanation.whyCorrect: Before any sex-specific differentiation, the mesonephric ducts work as part of the mesonephros, the embryonic kidney. When the mesonephros regresses, the ducts remain and retain the potential to form much of the male internal reproductive tract under the influence of testosterone.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The urogenital sinus is lined by endoderm derived from the cloaca, not by the mesonephric ducts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Anti-Müllerian hormone is secreted by Sertoli cells of the testis, not by the mesonephric ducts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Testosterone is produced by Leydig cells after testis formation, not by the ducts, and not during the indifferent stage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primordial germ cells migrate into the gonadal ridge on their own during the indifferent stage; the ducts do not carry them.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A newborn has ambiguous genitalia. Evaluation reveals incompletely developed gonads that produce limited but detectable amounts of sex hormones, with variable development of the internal ducts. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complete gonadal dysgenesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Müllerian agenesis (MRKH syndrome)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Partial (mixed) gonadal dysgenesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Persistent Müllerian duct syndrome

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prenatal diethylstilbestrol exposure
