explanation.summary: Partial (mixed) gonadal dysgenesis produces limited gonadal hormone production with ambiguous genitalia and variable development.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gonadal dysgenesis is impaired gonadal development causing decreased sex hormone production and abnormal differentiation. In the partial (mixed) form, the gonads develop incompletely and produce limited hormone, so the genitalia are ambiguous and duct development is variable, exactly as in this newborn.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Complete gonadal dysgenesis (e.g., 46,XY Swyer) produces nonfunctional streak gonads with a female phenotype and delayed puberty, not ambiguous genitalia with partial hormone production.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Müllerian agenesis is a female with absent uterus and upper vagina but normally functioning ovaries and unambiguous female genitalia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PMDS presents as a male with normal external genitalia who also has a uterus and uterine tubes, not ambiguous genitalia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: DES exposure alters Müllerian development in XX fetuses or feminizes XY fetuses; it does not cause incompletely developed, hormone-limited gonads.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A fetus produces neither anti-Müllerian hormone nor testosterone during the critical period after week 7. Which of the following outcomes is expected for the two paired duct systems?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both duct systems persist and differentiate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both duct systems regress completely

choices.label: C
choices.text: Duct fate is determined by the karyotype rather than hormones

choices.label: D
choices.text: Paramesonephric ducts persist; mesonephric ducts regress

choices.label: E
choices.text: Paramesonephric ducts regress; mesonephric ducts persist

explanation.summary: In the absence of AMH and testosterone, the paramesonephric ducts persist and the mesonephric ducts regress — the female duct pathway.
explanation.whyCorrect: Duct fate depends entirely on the hormonal environment after week 7. AMH is required to make the paramesonephric ducts regress, and testosterone is required to retain the mesonephric ducts. When neither hormone is present, the paramesonephric ducts persist to form the female internal tract while the mesonephric ducts regress.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Retention of both systems would require testosterone without AMH activity, as occurs in persistent Müllerian duct syndrome — not an absence of both hormones.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The paramesonephric ducts do not need any hormone to survive; they regress only when AMH acts on them.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The ducts of both systems are present in all embryos during weeks 4-6, and their pathways depend on the hormonal environment, not directly on the chromosomes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This is the male pattern, which requires both AMH (Müllerian regression) and testosterone (Wolffian retention).

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A 46,XY fetus forms testes in which the Sertoli cells function normally but the Leydig cells fail to produce hormone. Which of the following sets of internal findings is expected at birth?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absent epididymis and ductus deferens; uterus and tubes absent

choices.label: B
choices.text: Absent epididymis and ductus deferens; uterus and tubes present

choices.label: C
choices.text: Normal epididymis and ductus deferens; uterus absent

choices.label: D
choices.text: Normal epididymis and ductus deferens; uterus present

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streak gonads with neither duct system developed

explanation.summary: Sertoli-cell AMH still removes the Müllerian ducts, but without Leydig-cell testosterone the Wolffian ducts regress, leaving neither set of internal duct derivatives.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sertoli cells produce AMH, which causes the paramesonephric ducts to regress, so no uterus or uterine tubes form. Leydig cells produce the testosterone that supports mesonephric duct differentiation; without it, the mesonephric ducts regress, so the epididymis, ductus deferens, seminal vesicles, and ejaculatory ducts fail to develop.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Persistence of the uterus and tubes would mean AMH failed, but Sertoli cell function is intact in this fetus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The mesonephric-duct derivatives cannot develop normally without Leydig-cell testosterone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A retained uterus would require failed AMH signaling, but Sertoli cells function normally here; and Wolffian derivatives require testosterone, which is absent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streak gonads occur in gonadal dysgenesis; this fetus formed testes, with a selective Leydig cell defect.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: Primordial germ cells migrate into a developing testis during the indifferent stage. Which of the following best describes the subsequent behavior of these male germ cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are steadily depleted so that no germ cells remain at puberty

choices.label: B
choices.text: They arrest in prophase I from fetal life until puberty

choices.label: C
choices.text: They complete spermatogenesis before birth and then arrest

choices.label: D
choices.text: They proliferate extensively and begin meiosis during fetal life

choices.label: E
choices.text: They remain quiescent until puberty, then resume mitotic activity

explanation.summary: Male primordial germ cells stay quiescent throughout fetal and childhood development, resuming mitosis at puberty to enter spermatogenesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The primordial germ cells that migrate into the developing testis remain quiescent through fetal life and childhood. At puberty they resume mitotic activity and enter the pathway of spermatogenesis, ultimately giving rise to mature sperm capable of fertilization.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Male germ cells are preserved in a quiescent state and are the source of lifelong sperm production starting at puberty.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Arrest in prophase I as primary oocytes is the fate of female germ cells, not male germ cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Spermatogenesis does not begin until puberty; no sperm are made before birth.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Extensive fetal proliferation with entry into meiosis describes female germ cells in the fetal ovary, not male germ cells.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: The testes initially form high on the posterior abdominal wall and later descend into the scrotum. Which of the following is the primary reason this descent is necessary?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anti-Müllerian hormone production requires a scrotal position

choices.label: B
choices.text: Leydig cells secrete testosterone only at scrotal temperature

choices.label: C
choices.text: Normal spermatogenesis requires the cooler scrotal temperature

choices.label: D
choices.text: The gubernaculum cannot regress while inside the abdomen

choices.label: E
choices.text: The processus vaginalis must stay connected to the abdomen

explanation.summary: The testes must descend because the cooler temperature of the scrotum is required for normal spermatogenesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although the testes form high on the posterior abdominal wall, they must descend into the scrotum because its cooler temperature is required for normal spermatogenesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sertoli cells secrete AMH during fetal development before descent is complete; AMH does not depend on scrotal position.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Testosterone production is not the reason for descent; Leydig cells secrete testosterone during fetal life while the testes are still intra-abdominal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The gubernaculum regresses after guiding descent; its regression is a consequence of descent, not the reason for it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The proximal connection of the processus vaginalis to the abdomen normally closes after descent; maintaining it is not a goal of descent.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: During fetal development, the testis moves from the lumbar region down to the deep inguinal ring before it ever enters the inguinal canal. Which of the following mechanisms accounts for this first stage of descent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elongation of the processus vaginalis pushing the testis caudally

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enlargement of the abdomen and pelvis while the testis stays anchored

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rapid growth of the testis itself propelling it toward the pelvis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Regression of the mesonephros releasing the testis from the body wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Traction by the gubernaculum pulling the testis through the canal

explanation.summary: The first part of testicular descent is relative: the abdomen and pelvis enlarge while the testis remains anchored in place.
explanation.whyCorrect: Descent from the lumbar region to the deep inguinal ring occurs mainly because the abdomen and pelvis enlarge while the testes remain anchored in place. The testis therefore ends up relatively lower without being actively pulled during this stage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The processus vaginalis is a peritoneal pouch that accompanies the testis; it does not push the testis downward.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Growth of the testis itself is not described as a force of descent; the mechanism is differential growth of the abdomen and pelvis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mesonephric regression leaves the mesonephric ducts behind but is not the mechanism of the first stage of descent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gubernacular guidance through the inguinal canal into the scrotum is the second part of descent, beginning around week 26.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: Around week 26, a fibrous cord attached to the testis and the labioscrotal swellings guides the testis through the inguinal canal into the scrotum. After descent is complete, this cord normally undergoes which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Closure of its connection to the abdominal cavity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Differentiation into the epididymis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Division into two pelvic ligaments

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gradual regression

choices.label: E
choices.text: Persistence as the tunica vaginalis

explanation.summary: In males, the gubernaculum guides the testis into the scrotum and then gradually regresses.
explanation.whyCorrect: The gubernaculum is the fibrous cord attaching the testis to the labioscrotal swellings; beginning around week 26 it guides the testis through the inguinal canal into the scrotum. After descent, the gubernaculum gradually regresses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Closure of the proximal connection to the abdomen is the fate of the processus vaginalis, not of the gubernaculum.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The epididymis is a mesonephric-duct derivative and is unrelated to the gubernaculum.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Division into the ovarian ligament and round ligament of the uterus is the fate of the female gubernaculum, not the male one.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The tunica vaginalis derives from the distal processus vaginalis, a peritoneal pouch, not from the gubernaculum.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A pouch of peritoneum accompanies the testis during its descent into the scrotum. After descent is complete, which of the following normally happens to the proximal portion of this pouch?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It differentiates into the ejaculatory duct

choices.label: B
choices.text: It persists as the tunica vaginalis of the testis

choices.label: C
choices.text: It remains widely open into the abdominal cavity

choices.label: D
choices.text: It thickens into the gubernaculum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Its connection to the abdominal cavity closes

explanation.summary: The proximal processus vaginalis normally closes off its connection to the abdominal cavity after testicular descent; only the distal portion persists as the tunica vaginalis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The processus vaginalis is the peritoneal pouch that accompanies the descending testis. Its distal portion becomes the tunica vaginalis, while the proximal connection to the abdomen normally closes after descent is complete.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The ejaculatory ducts are mesonephric-duct derivatives, unrelated to the peritoneal pouch.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The tunica vaginalis forms from the distal portion of the processus vaginalis, not the proximal portion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Remaining open is not the normal outcome; the proximal connection normally closes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The gubernaculum is a separate fibrous cord that guides descent and regresses; it is not derived from peritoneum.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: The prostate and the pelvic urethra arise from the endoderm of the urogenital sinus. The urogenital sinus itself forms as a result of which of the following embryonic events?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Caudal growth of the mesonephric ducts toward the pelvis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Division of the cloaca into urogenital and anorectal passages

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fusion of the caudal paramesonephric ducts at the midline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fusion of the urogenital folds at the ventral midline

choices.label: E
choices.text: Regression of the mesonephros and its tubules

explanation.summary: The urogenital sinus forms when the embryonic cloaca divides into separate urogenital and anorectal passages, the sinus deriving from the ventral division.
explanation.whyCorrect: The urogenital sinus arises when the cloaca divides into a urogenital passage and an anorectal passage; the sinus derives from the ventral division of the cloaca. Its endoderm then gives rise to the prostate and urethra in males and the lower vagina in females.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The mesonephric ducts grow toward the pelvis as duct structures; they do not form the urogenital sinus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fusion of the caudal paramesonephric ducts forms the uterus, cervix, and upper vagina, not the urogenital sinus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ventral midline fusion of the urogenital folds forms the penile urethra later in development.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mesonephric regression leaves the mesonephric ducts behind; it does not create the urogenital sinus.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A researcher compares germ cell behavior in fetal gonads of both sexes. Compared with germ cells in the fetal testis, germ cells in the fetal ovary differ in which of the following ways?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They arrest in metaphase II of meiosis II shortly before birth

choices.label: B
choices.text: They continue generating new gametes from stem cells throughout adult life

choices.label: C
choices.text: They migrate into the gonadal ridge only in the weeks after birth

choices.label: D
choices.text: They proliferate extensively and each begins meiosis in fetal life

choices.label: E
choices.text: They remain quiescent until puberty and then divide continuously

explanation.summary: Pronounced proliferation of primordial germ cells occurs in the fetal ovary, where each cell begins meiosis and arrests in prophase I; male germ cells instead stay quiescent until puberty.
explanation.whyCorrect: In XX embryos, primordial germ cells proliferate extensively during fetal life and each one begins meiosis, then arrests in prophase I as a primary oocyte. This contrasts with the fetal testis, in which primordial germ cells remain quiescent until puberty and then resume mitotic activity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fetal oocytes arrest in prophase I of meiosis I, not metaphase II.
whyWrongByChoice.B: No new oocytes are produced after birth; the pool of primary oocytes is fixed. Ongoing gamete production is a male feature.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Primordial germ cells migrate into the gonadal ridge during the indifferent stage of embryonic development, not after birth.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Quiescence until puberty describes male germ cells; ovarian germ cells are highly active during fetal life.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A 49-year-old woman who is pregnant asks how her age affects the chance that her child will have Down syndrome. Which of the following is the approximate risk at her age?

choices.label: C
choices.text: 1 in 26

choices.label: D
choices.text: 1 in 5

explanation.summary: Down syndrome risk climbs steeply with maternal age, reaching about 1 in 26 by age 49.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because primary oocytes remain arrested in prophase I for decades, the risk of nondisjunction and resulting aneuploidy rises with maternal age. For Down syndrome the approximate risks are 1 in 1,500 at age 18, 1 in 695 at age 32, and 1 in 26 at age 49.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 1 in 1,500 is the approximate risk at age 18, not at 49.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 1 in 250 understates the risk at age 49, which is roughly tenfold higher.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 1 in 5 overstates the risk; at age 49 it is about 1 in 26.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 1 in 695 is the approximate risk at age 32, not at 49.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman receives preconception counseling about aneuploidies whose risk rises with maternal age because of nondisjunction in oocytes long arrested in prophase I. In addition to Down syndrome, this mechanism increases the risk of which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complete and partial gonadal dysgenesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cryptorchidism and transverse testicular ectopia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Müllerian agenesis and persistent Müllerian duct syndrome

choices.label: D
choices.text: T-shaped uterus and vaginal adenosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Turner syndrome and Klinefelter syndrome

explanation.summary: Age-related nondisjunction causes aneuploidies including trisomy 21, Turner syndrome (monosomy X), and Klinefelter syndrome (XXY).
explanation.whyCorrect: Increased nondisjunction in long-arrested primary oocytes produces more aneuploidy, increasing chromosomal disorders such as Down syndrome (trisomy 21), Turner syndrome (monosomy X), and Klinefelter syndrome (XXY).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gonadal dysgenesis is impaired gonadal development, not an aneuploidy produced by age-related meiotic error.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cryptorchidism and transverse testicular ectopia are features associated with persistent Müllerian duct syndrome, not chromosomal nondisjunction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Müllerian agenesis and PMDS are developmental duct disorders (failed Müllerian development and failed Müllerian regression), not aneuploidies from nondisjunction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: T-shaped uterus and vaginal adenosis are consequences of prenatal DES exposure in XX fetuses, not maternal-age aneuploidies.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A child is diagnosed with Prader-Willi syndrome caused by maternal uniparental disomy rather than a deletion. Which of the following maternal factors is a significant risk factor for this subtype?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Advanced maternal age

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prenatal androgen excess

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prenatal anti-androgen exposure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prenatal diethylstilbestrol exposure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Young maternal age at conception

explanation.summary: Advanced maternal age is a significant risk factor for the maternal uniparental disomy (mUPD) subtype of imprinting disorders such as Prader-Willi syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Advanced maternal age is a significant risk factor for the mUPD subtype of Prader-Willi syndrome. Matsubara et al. (2011) reported a median maternal age difference of approximately seven years between mUPD cases and deletion cases of PWS, with mUPD mothers being older.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Androgen excess virilizes XX external genitalia; it is not linked to uniparental disomy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Anti-androgen exposure impairs virilization of XY fetuses; it is not linked to uniparental disomy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: DES is an endocrine disruptor affecting Müllerian development and virilization; it is not the risk factor for mUPD imprinting disorders.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The maternal age association runs the other way: mUPD mothers were older, by a median of about seven years, than deletion-case mothers.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: In a 46,XX fetus, the mesonephric (Wolffian) ducts regress during development. The absence of which of the following directly accounts for this regression?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anti-Müllerian hormone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dihydrotestosterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estrogen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Functional AMH receptors

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testosterone

explanation.summary: Without Leydig cells, XX embryos lack significant testosterone, and without testosterone the mesonephric ducts regress.
explanation.whyCorrect: Testosterone is the hormone that causes the mesonephric ducts to be retained and differentiate. Because Leydig cells are not present in XX embryos, significant levels of testosterone are not produced, and the mesonephric ducts therefore regress.

whyWrongByChoice.A: AMH governs the paramesonephric ducts (causing their regression); its absence in females allows the Müllerian ducts to persist but has no role in Wolffian regression.
whyWrongByChoice.B: DHT drives differentiation of the male external genitalia; mesonephric duct retention depends on testosterone itself.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Estrogen from the fetal ovaries supports female external genital development; it does not maintain or eliminate the mesonephric ducts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: AMH receptor function determines whether the Müllerian ducts regress, as in persistent Müllerian duct syndrome; it does not affect the mesonephric ducts.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: Expectant parents ask when their fetus's external genitalia will have finished developing a clearly male or female form. Differentiation of the external genitalia begins around week 9. By approximately which week is it usually complete?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Week 10

choices.label: B
choices.text: Week 11

choices.label: C
choices.text: Week 12

choices.label: D
choices.text: Week 16

choices.label: E
choices.text: Week 20

explanation.summary: External genital differentiation begins around week 9 and is usually complete by week 12.
explanation.whyCorrect: At week 8 the external genitalia are still undifferentiated and identical in both sexes. By week 9 the genital tubercle, urogenital folds, and labioscrotal swellings begin differentiating into male or female structures, and full differentiation is usually complete by week 12.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Week 10 is too early; differentiation has only recently begun and is not usually complete.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Week 11 is still within the window of active differentiation, which usually finishes by week 12.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Week 16 is later than the usual completion point of week 12.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Week 20 is well past the usual completion of external genital differentiation.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: In a female fetus, one of the three shared external genital precursors gives rise to the glans clitoris and part of the clitoral body. In a male fetus, this same precursor gives rise to which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glans penis and most of the penile shaft

choices.label: B
choices.text: The bulbourethral (Cowper) glands

choices.label: C
choices.text: The lining of the penile (spongy) urethra

choices.label: D
choices.text: The prostate gland and its glandular ducts

choices.label: E
choices.text: The scrotal skin and underlying dartos

explanation.summary: The genital tubercle forms the glans clitoris and part of the clitoral body in females and the glans penis and most of the penile shaft in males.
explanation.whyCorrect: The precursor described is the genital tubercle, one of the three undifferentiated external structures present at week 8. In males it becomes the glans penis and most of the penile shaft; in females it becomes the glans clitoris and part of the clitoral body, making these structures homologs.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The bulbourethral glands arise from the urogenital sinus; their female homologs are the greater vestibular glands.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The penile urethra forms when the urogenital folds fuse along the ventral midline, not from the genital tubercle.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The prostate arises from the urogenital sinus; its female homologs are the urethral and paraurethral glands.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The scrotum arises from the labioscrotal swellings, whose female homolog is the labia majora.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: During male development, the pelvic portions of the urethra form directly from the urogenital sinus, but the penile urethra forms later. Which of the following processes creates the penile urethra?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Canalization of a solid cord within the center of the genital tubercle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Caudal extension of the paired mesonephric ducts into the phallus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fusion of the urogenital folds along the ventral midline of the penis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Midline fusion of the paired labioscrotal swellings beneath the phallus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Regression of a temporary midline septum within the body of the phallus

explanation.summary: The penile urethra is created when the urogenital folds fuse along the ventral midline of the developing penis.
explanation.whyCorrect: As the penis develops from the genital tubercle, the urogenital folds fuse along its ventral midline to create the penile urethra. This contrasts with the pelvic portions of the male urethra, which form directly from the urogenital sinus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The genital tubercle forms the glans and most of the penile shaft; the urethra is not made by hollowing out the tubercle.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The mesonephric ducts form the SEED structures (seminal vesicles, epididymis, ejaculatory ducts, ductus deferens), not the penile urethra.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Midline fusion of the labioscrotal swellings forms the scrotum, not the urethra.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Regression of a midline septum describes the uterovaginal septum in females, not penile urethral formation.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: The bulbourethral glands in males arise from the urogenital sinus. Which of the following female structures shares this same embryologic origin as their homolog?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Greater vestibular glands

choices.label: B
choices.text: Labia majora

choices.label: C
choices.text: Labia minora

choices.label: D
choices.text: Upper vagina

choices.label: E
choices.text: Urethral and paraurethral glands

explanation.summary: The male bulbourethral glands and the female greater vestibular glands are urogenital sinus homologs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the internal structures arising from the urogenital sinus, the male bulbourethral glands correspond to the female greater vestibular glands. These pairs share the same embryologic origin even though they differ in adult form.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The labia majora derive from the labioscrotal swellings, homologous to the scrotum.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The labia minora derive from the urogenital folds, homologous to the tissue forming the penile urethra.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The upper vagina arises from the fused caudal paramesonephric ducts, not from the urogenital sinus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The urethral and paraurethral glands are also urogenital sinus derivatives, but they are the female homologs of the prostate, not of the bulbourethral glands.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A student is reviewing how the urethra develops in each sex. Which of the following statements about urethral development is accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In both sexes the urethra develops from the urogenital sinus

choices.label: B
choices.text: The female urethra derives from the paramesonephric ducts

choices.label: C
choices.text: The female urethra opens between the labia majora

choices.label: D
choices.text: The male pelvic urethra forms from the genital tubercle

choices.label: E
choices.text: The urethra functions as a reproductive organ in both sexes

explanation.summary: The urethra develops from the urogenital sinus in both sexes, although it is part of the reproductive system only in males.
explanation.whyCorrect: In both males and females, the urethra develops from the urogenital sinus. In females the short urethra remains in the pelvis and opens between the labia minora; in males the pelvic portions form directly from the urogenital sinus and the penile portion forms as the urogenital folds fuse on the ventral penis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The female urethra comes from the urogenital sinus; the paramesonephric ducts form the uterine tubes, uterus, and upper vagina.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The female urethra opens into the external genital region between the labia minora, not the labia majora.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The male pelvic urethra forms directly from the urogenital sinus; the genital tubercle forms the glans and most of the penile shaft.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The urethra is part of the reproductive system in males but not in females.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman learns that her mother was prescribed a synthetic estrogen, diethylstilbestrol (DES), during the pregnancy. Which of the following sets of findings is characteristic of prenatal DES exposure in a 46,XX fetus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absent uterus and upper vagina with normal ovaries

choices.label: B
choices.text: Persistent uterovaginal septum dividing a duplicated uterus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Streak gonads with delayed puberty and a female phenotype

choices.label: D
choices.text: T-shaped uterus and vaginal adenosis with normal ovaries

choices.label: E
choices.text: Virilized external genitalia with normal internal organs

explanation.summary: Prenatal DES exposure in XX fetuses causes abnormal Müllerian development, producing a T-shaped uterus and vaginal adenosis while the ovaries remain normal.
explanation.whyCorrect: DES is a synthetic estrogen that acts as an endocrine disruptor, altering estrogen-dependent gene expression. In XX fetuses it causes abnormal Müllerian development, resulting in a T-shaped uterus and vaginal adenosis; the ovaries are normal because DES targets duct development rather than the gonad.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An absent uterus and upper vagina with normal ovaries describes Müllerian agenesis (MRKH syndrome), not DES exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The uterovaginal septum normally regresses during paramesonephric fusion; a persistent dividing septum is not the described DES lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Streak gonads with delayed puberty describe complete gonadal dysgenesis, not an estrogenic teratogen effect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Virilization of the external genitalia with normal internal organs is the effect of androgen excess in XX fetuses, not DES.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A couple undergoing fertility evaluation reports that the male partner's mother took diethylstilbestrol (DES) while pregnant with him. Which of the following sets of findings is characteristic of prenatal DES exposure in a 46,XY fetus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both testes descended into the same side of the scrotum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cryptorchidism, epididymal abnormalities, and reduced spermatogenesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: No abnormalities, because XY fetuses resist excess estrogen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Retained uterus and uterine tubes with normal virilization

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streak gonads with a completely female external phenotype

explanation.summary: In XY fetuses, excess estrogen from DES causes feminization with impaired virilization: cryptorchidism, epididymal abnormalities, and reduced spermatogenesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Prenatal DES exposure delivers excess estrogen to the XY fetus, causing feminization characterized by impaired virilization. The characteristic findings are cryptorchidism, epididymal abnormalities, and reduced spermatogenesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both testes descending on the same side (transverse testicular ectopia) is a sign associated with persistent Müllerian duct syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.C: XY fetuses are not resistant to excess estrogen; DES causes feminization with impaired virilization.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A retained uterus and tubes in an otherwise normal male describes persistent Müllerian duct syndrome from abnormal AMH or AMH receptors, not DES exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streak gonads with a female phenotype describe complete gonadal dysgenesis (e.g., 46,XY Swyer), not a teratogenic estrogen effect.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: During the masculinization programming window, a 46,XY fetus is exposed to a significant excess of androgens acting through androgen receptor signaling. Which of the following outcomes is expected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Feminized external genitalia with bilateral cryptorchidism

choices.label: B
choices.text: Minimal effect, given the already high-androgen environment

choices.label: C
choices.text: Persistence of the paramesonephric ducts with a uterus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduced spermatogenesis with epididymal cysts and abnormalities

choices.label: E
choices.text: Regression of the mesonephric ducts before differentiation

explanation.summary: Androgen excess has minimal effect on XY fetuses because their environment is already androgen-rich; it is XX fetuses that become virilized.
explanation.whyCorrect: Androgen exposure affects sex differentiation via androgen receptor signaling during the masculinization programming window. In XY fetuses, excess androgen has minimal effect because the fetus already develops in a high-androgen environment. By contrast, in XX fetuses androgen excess virilizes the external genitalia (clitoromegaly, labial fusion) while internal organs remain normal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Feminization with cryptorchidism is the effect of excess estrogen (e.g., DES) or would follow anti-androgen exposure, which has effects opposite to androgen excess.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Paramesonephric regression depends on AMH, which androgens do not block; excess androgen does not cause Müllerian persistence in an XY fetus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reduced spermatogenesis and epididymal abnormalities characterize prenatal DES (estrogen) exposure in XY fetuses, not androgen excess.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Testosterone maintains the mesonephric ducts; extra androgen would not cause them to regress.

questions.topicName: Sex Determination and Reproductive Systems Development

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman is evaluated after two first-trimester pregnancy losses. Hysterosalpingography shows a single uterine cavity divided by a midline partition, with the two cavities meeting at an acute angle. Additional imaging confirms a normal external fundal contour, and septoplasty is recommended. Failure of which of the following developmental processes most likely caused this patient's condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Development of the lower vagina from the urogenital sinus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fusion of the paramesonephric ducts along their entire length

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fusion of the paramesonephric ducts in the fundic region

choices.label: D
choices.text: Regression of the mesonephric ducts in the female fetus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Resorption of the uterovaginal septum after duct fusion

explanation.summary: A septate uterus results when the paramesonephric ducts fuse normally but the uterovaginal septum fails to resorb.
explanation.whyCorrect: The normal fundal contour with an internally divided cavity is the hallmark of a septate uterus: fusion occurred, but the temporary midline uterovaginal septum was not resorbed, leaving a fibrous or muscular septum. This is the anomaly correctable by septoplasty, which improves reproductive outcomes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Failure of the lower vagina to form from the urogenital sinus causes vaginal atresia, not a divided uterine cavity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Complete fusion failure produces uterus didelphys, with two separate uteri and typically two cervices, not a single externally normal uterus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Partial fundal fusion failure produces a bicornuate uterus, which has a divided, horned external contour and a wider angle between cavities on HSG.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A persistent mesonephric remnant produces a Gartner cyst on the lateral vaginal wall and does not alter the uterine cavity.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman undergoes imaging during an infertility workup. The uterine fundus is divided into two horn-like superior cavities that meet at a wide angle, while the lower uterine segment, cervix, and vagina are normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bicornuate uterus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gartner duct cyst

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mullerian agenesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Septate uterus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uterus didelphys

explanation.summary: A bicornuate uterus reflects partial failure of paramesonephric duct fusion confined to the fundic region.
explanation.whyCorrect: Two horn-like fundic cavities with a normal lower uterus, cervix, and vagina define a bicornuate uterus, named for its two unfused superior horns. On imaging the angle between the two cavities is wider than the acute angle of a septate uterus.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A Gartner cyst is a mesonephric remnant on the lateral vaginal wall and does not change uterine shape.
whyWrongByChoice.C: In Mullerian agenesis (MRKH) the uterus and upper vagina are absent, not duplicated at the fundus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A septate uterus has a normal external contour with an internal septum, and the cavities meet at an acute rather than wide angle.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uterus didelphys results from complete fusion failure, producing two separate uteri and typically two cervices, not a single lower uterus.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A 13-year-old girl has monthly episodes of lower abdominal pain but has never menstruated. She has Tanner stage 4 breast development. Examination shows a bulging, bluish membrane at the vaginal introitus and a palpable suprapubic mass. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Excision of a lateral vaginal wall cyst

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hysteroscopic septoplasty

choices.label: C
choices.text: Incision of the hymenal membrane

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reassurance and repeat examination in one year

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surgical creation of a neovagina

explanation.summary: Imperforate hymen causes primary amenorrhea with cyclic pain and hematocolpos, treated by hymenotomy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cyclic pain, normal secondary sexual characteristics, and a bulging bluish membrane at the introitus indicate menstrual blood trapped behind an imperforate hymen (hematocolpos, with possible hematometra). Surgical incision of the hymen relieves the obstruction and restores normal menstrual outflow.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Excision treats a symptomatic Gartner cyst, which sits on the lateral vaginal wall and does not obstruct menstrual flow.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Septoplasty corrects a septate uterus; it does not address an obstructed vaginal opening.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Observation leaves the obstruction in place, allowing continued accumulation of blood and risk of urinary retention from compression.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vaginal reconstruction addresses vaginal atresia or agenesis; this patient has a normally developed vagina behind the hymen.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A 17-year-old girl is evaluated for primary amenorrhea. She has normal breast development and pubic hair. Pelvic examination shows normal external genitalia with a short, blind-ending lower vagina. Ultrasonography shows normal ovaries but no uterus. Karyotype is 46,XX. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complete androgen insensitivity syndrome

choices.label: C
choices.text: Imperforate hymen with hematocolpos

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mayer-von Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser syndrome

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uterus didelphys with double cervix

explanation.summary: MRKH syndrome (Mullerian agenesis) is failure of the paramesonephric ducts to form, leaving no uterus or upper vagina in a 46,XX female with normal ovaries.
explanation.whyCorrect: In MRKH syndrome the Mullerian ducts fail to develop normally, so the uterus and upper vagina are absent while the lower vagina, ovaries, and external genitalia are normal. It is typically diagnosed when a girl fails to menstruate, and the 46,XX karyotype with normal ovaries fits this diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CAH virilizes the external genitalia of a 46,XX fetus; it does not cause absence of the uterus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Complete AIS occurs in 46,XY individuals with testes; this patient is 46,XX with ovaries.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An imperforate hymen obstructs an otherwise normally developed uterus and vagina and causes cyclic pain with hematocolpos, not an absent uterus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uterus didelphys is duplication of the uterus from complete fusion failure, the opposite of agenesis.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A male infant born at 34 weeks' gestation has an empty right hemiscrotum, with a smooth mass palpable in the right inguinal region. The testis has not descended by 18 months of age and the family declines surgery. Which of the following best explains the mechanism by which this condition threatens future fertility?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Leydig cells stop producing testosterone outside the scrotum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Peritoneal fluid compresses the seminiferous tubules

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sertoli cell function is impaired at core body temperature

choices.label: D
choices.text: Target tissues become resistant to circulating androgens

choices.label: E
choices.text: The vas deferens fails to form on the affected side

explanation.summary: Undescended testes sit at core body temperature, where temperature-sensitive Sertoli cells cannot support sperm maturation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Scrotal temperature is normally lower than core body temperature. In cryptorchidism the testis remains in the abdomen or inguinal canal, and the temperature-sensitive Sertoli cells responsible for sperm maturation do not function optimally at core temperature, producing infertility; the disrupted germ cell differentiation also raises germ cell tumor risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The lecture attributes infertility in cryptorchidism to Sertoli cell temperature sensitivity affecting sperm maturation, not loss of Leydig hormone production.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Peritoneal fluid tracking into the scrotum describes a communicating hydrocele, not the mechanism of infertility in cryptorchidism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Androgen receptor resistance is the mechanism of androgen insensitivity syndrome, unrelated to testicular position.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Absence of the vas deferens is a separate anomaly related to CFTR mutations, not a consequence of failed testicular descent.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A 4-month-old boy has painless swelling of the left hemiscrotum. Ultrasonography shows an anechoic fluid collection surrounding the testis, and the swelling has persisted since birth with fluctuation in size. The processus vaginalis is found to be widely patent. In addition to the current findings, this patient is at greatest risk for which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bladder exstrophy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Indirect inguinal hernia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obstructive azoospermia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Penile fibrous plaque formation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testicular germ cell tumor

explanation.summary: A widely patent processus vaginalis underlies a communicating hydrocele and increases the risk of indirect inguinal hernia.
explanation.whyCorrect: A communicating hydrocele results from incomplete closure of the processus vaginalis, allowing peritoneal fluid into the tunica vaginalis. When the processus vaginalis is widely patent, abdominal contents can also pass through it, so these patients are at increased risk of developing an indirect inguinal hernia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bladder exstrophy is associated with epispadias and failed midline abdominal wall closure, not with hydrocele.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Obstructive azoospermia results from congenital absence of the vas deferens, not from a patent processus vaginalis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fibrous plaques of the erectile tissue describe Peyronie disease, an acquired adult condition unrelated to hydrocele.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Germ cell tumor risk is a sequela of cryptorchidism, in which the testis remains at higher temperature; this testis is descended.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A newborn boy has a urethral opening on the ventral surface of the penile shaft, proximal to the glans. The foreskin has a hooded appearance with absent ventral tissue, and the penis curves ventrally. Which of the following developmental abnormalities most likely produced these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abnormally dorsal positioning of the genital tubercle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Failure of midline closure of the anterior abdominal wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: Failure of the testes to descend into the scrotum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Incomplete fusion of the urogenital folds

choices.label: E
choices.text: Persistence of the processus vaginalis after testicular descent

explanation.summary: Hypospadias results from failure of the urethral folds to fuse completely along the ventral midline.
explanation.whyCorrect: A ventral urethral opening with a hooded, cobra-head foreskin and chordee (congenital ventral curvature) is classic for hypospadias, the most common congenital penile anomaly. It reflects incomplete fusion of the urethral folds during formation of the penile urethra.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dorsal malposition of the genital tubercle causes epispadias, with a dorsal rather than ventral urethral opening.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Failed midline abdominal wall closure causes bladder exstrophy, which is associated with epispadias.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Failed testicular descent is cryptorchidism, which presents with an empty scrotal sac.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A persistent processus vaginalis produces a communicating hydrocele, not an abnormal urethral meatus.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A newborn boy is noted to have the urethral meatus located on the dorsal surface of the penis rather than at the tip of the glans. This anomaly is most frequently associated with which of the following conditions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bladder exstrophy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Communicating hydrocele

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cryptorchidism

choices.label: D
choices.text: Peyronie disease

choices.label: E
choices.text: Unilateral renal agenesis

explanation.summary: Epispadias is frequently associated with bladder exstrophy because both reflect extensive disruption of midline development.
explanation.whyCorrect: A dorsal urethral opening defines epispadias, which arises when the genital tubercle develops in an abnormally dorsal position. Epispadias is much less common than hypospadias and is frequently associated with bladder exstrophy, in which the bladder is exposed on the anterior abdominal wall from failure of midline closure.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A communicating hydrocele arises from a patent processus vaginalis and is not linked to epispadias.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cryptorchidism reflects failed testicular descent and is associated with prematurity, not with dorsal urethral malposition.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Peyronie disease is an acquired adult condition of fibrous plaques in erectile tissue, unrelated to this congenital anomaly.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Unilateral renal agenesis is described in association with congenital absence of the vas deferens, not epispadias.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man is evaluated for infertility. Semen analysis on two occasions shows azoospermia. He has normal testicular size, normal secondary sexual characteristics, and a normal serum testosterone concentration, but the vas deferens is not palpable on either side. Mutation of which of the following genes is the most likely cause of his condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A gene controlling gonadal differentiation

choices.label: B
choices.text: A gene disrupted by trinucleotide repeat expansion

choices.label: C
choices.text: AR

choices.label: D
choices.text: CFTR

choices.label: E
choices.text: The gene encoding 21-hydroxylase

explanation.summary: Congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens is classically caused by CFTR mutations, producing obstructive azoospermia with preserved spermatogenesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: In CFTR-related disease, abnormal ion transport during embryogenesis leads to failure of normal formation or early degeneration of the vas deferens. Affected men present in adulthood with infertility from obstructive azoospermia, yet spermatogenesis, testicular size, secondary sexual characteristics, and testosterone are normal; sperm retrieval with IVF or ICSI can allow biological fatherhood.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Disordered gonadal differentiation produces ovotesticular DSD; this patient has normal testes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A trinucleotide repeat in the androgen receptor causes Kennedy disease, which presents with progressive weakness and gynecomastia, not absent vasa.
whyWrongByChoice.C: AR mutations cause androgen insensitivity, in which 46,XY individuals develop female or ambiguous external genitalia; this man is normally virilized.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 21-hydroxylase deficiency causes congenital adrenal hyperplasia with virilization of XX fetuses, not isolated absence of the vas deferens.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A newborn with a 46,XX karyotype has virilized external genitalia. Ultrasonography shows ovaries and a uterus, with no testicular tissue identified. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this infant's condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 21-hydroxylase deficiency increasing fetal androgen production

choices.label: B
choices.text: Androgen receptor mutation preventing testosterone action

choices.label: C
choices.text: Complete failure of paramesonephric duct fusion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Persistence of a mesonephric duct remnant

choices.label: E
choices.text: Presence of both ovarian and testicular tissue in the gonads

explanation.summary: The most common cause of 46,XX DSD is congenital adrenal hyperplasia from 21-hydroxylase deficiency, which virilizes a genetically female fetus.
explanation.whyCorrect: In 46,XX DSD, a female genotype with ovaries develops male or ambiguous external genitalia because of excess androgen exposure in utero. The most common cause is CAH from 21-hydroxylase deficiency: impaired cortisol synthesis drives increased androgen production, virilizing the external genitalia. Teratogenic androgen exposure or maternal tumors can do the same.

whyWrongByChoice.B: AR mutations cause under-virilization of 46,XY individuals (androgen insensitivity), not virilization of a 46,XX fetus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Complete fusion failure of the paramesonephric ducts causes uterus didelphys, a structural uterine anomaly without virilization.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A mesonephric remnant produces a Gartner cyst on the vaginal wall and does not virilize external genitalia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ovotesticular DSD requires both ovarian and testicular tissue; imaging here shows no testicular tissue.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A 16-year-old phenotypic female is evaluated for primary amenorrhea. Examination shows normal-appearing female external genitalia. Bilateral inguinal masses are identified as testes on imaging, karyotype is 46,XY, and the serum testosterone concentration is in the normal male range. Which of the following best explains this patient's phenotype?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abnormal ion transport degraded the mesonephric duct derivatives

choices.label: B
choices.text: Target tissues cannot respond to circulating testosterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: The adrenal glands overproduce androgen precursors

choices.label: D
choices.text: The gonads contain both ovarian and testicular tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: The testes are unable to synthesize testosterone

explanation.summary: In androgen insensitivity syndrome, androgen receptor mutations leave target tissues unable to respond to testosterone, so external genitalia follow the default female pattern.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is 46,XY DSD from androgen insensitivity syndrome, the most common cause. Testosterone is produced by the testes, and levels are normal, but mutations in the androgen receptor prevent target tissues from responding, so external genital development follows the default female pattern. Complete and partial forms exist.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CFTR-related degeneration of the vas deferens causes obstructive azoospermia in normally virilized men, not a female phenotype.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Adrenal androgen excess (CAH) virilizes 46,XX fetuses; it would not feminize a 46,XY individual with normal testosterone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ovotesticular DSD involves both gonadal tissue types, most often with a 46,XX karyotype; imaging here shows testes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Defective testosterone synthesis, as in rare forms of CAH, causes under-virilization with low androgen production, but this patient's testosterone is normal.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A newborn has ambiguous genitalia, and evaluation at a quaternary center with a multidisciplinary team is arranged. The parents request genital surgery before hospital discharge to spare the child distress, while several team members recommend waiting. Which of the following best characterizes the central ethical tension in this decision?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Achieving surgical precision in the newborn versus limiting cumulative anesthesia exposure in infancy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Confirming a precise genetic diagnosis versus beginning any supportive care at all

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deciding which single specialist should direct the treatment plan rather than the team

choices.label: D
choices.text: Early intervention to relieve ambiguity versus deferring surgery to preserve the patient's autonomy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Protecting the patient's future confidentiality versus informing the extended family now

explanation.summary: The key ethical tension in DSD management is between early intervention and deferring irreversible decisions until the patient can exercise autonomy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Management of DSDs is guided by autonomy, benevolence, non-maleficence, and justice, and the central unresolved tension is between the desire for early intervention (to relieve the angst of ambiguity and achieve better surgical outcomes) and patient autonomy, which would require deferring intervention until adulthood. Care should be individualized by a multidisciplinary team with the family, incorporating the patient's cultural setting.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anesthesia exposure is not the ethical dilemma the lecture identifies; the conflict concerns timing of irreversible intervention versus self-determination.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Supportive care is not withheld pending genetic results; sequencing diagnosis against support is not the described tension.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Care is delivered cooperatively by a multidisciplinary team with the family, not directed by a single lead specialist.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Confidentiality versus family disclosure is not the central conflict described in DSD management.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman presents for a routine examination. Speculum examination shows two cervices separated by a longitudinal vaginal septum. MRI of the pelvis shows two widely separated uterine bodies, each with its own cavity and its own cervix. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bicornuate uterus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Imperforate hymen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mullerian agenesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Septate uterus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uterus didelphys

explanation.summary: Uterus didelphys is complete failure of paramesonephric duct fusion, producing two separate uteri, typically two cervices, and often a duplicated vagina.
explanation.whyCorrect: Two entirely separate uterine bodies, two cervices, and a duplicated vagina indicate that the paramesonephric ducts never fused at any level. Fertility may be preserved, but the condition carries an increased risk of miscarriage, preterm delivery, and fetal malpresentation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A bicornuate uterus has two fundic horns but a normal single lower uterus, cervix, and vagina, because fusion failed only in the fundic region.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An imperforate hymen obstructs an otherwise normally formed single vagina and uterus; it does not duplicate them.
whyWrongByChoice.C: In Mullerian agenesis (MRKH syndrome) the uterus and upper vagina are absent, not duplicated.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A septate uterus is a single fused uterus with one cervix, divided internally by an unresorbed uterovaginal septum.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman is diagnosed with a septate uterus during an infertility evaluation and asks how the anomaly could affect a future pregnancy. In addition to miscarriage and preterm labor, her condition places a pregnancy at increased risk for which of the following complications?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ectopic implantation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fetal malpresentation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gestational hypertension

choices.label: D
choices.text: Polyhydramnios

choices.label: E
choices.text: Postpartum hemorrhage

explanation.summary: A septate uterus permits pregnancy but increases the risk of miscarriage, preterm labor, and fetal malpresentation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The internal septum distorts the uterine cavity, and the lecture links a septate uterus specifically to miscarriage, preterm labor, and fetal malpresentation. Because the external contour is normal, septoplasty can correct the anomaly and improve reproductive outcomes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ectopic implantation is not among the obstetric risks attributed to a septate uterus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gestational hypertension is not a described consequence of paramesonephric fusion or resorption anomalies.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Polyhydramnios is unrelated to the cavity distortion caused by a retained uterovaginal septum.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Postpartum hemorrhage is not one of the complications linked to a septate uterus.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman reports discomfort during intercourse. Pelvic examination shows a 3-cm smooth cyst along the lateral wall of the vagina; the uterus, cervix, and ovaries are normal. This lesion is most likely a remnant of which of the following embryonic structures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hymenal membrane

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mesonephric duct

choices.label: C
choices.text: Paramesonephric duct

choices.label: D
choices.text: Urogenital sinus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uterovaginal septum

explanation.summary: A Gartner cyst is a persistent remnant of the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct on the lateral vaginal wall.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gartner cysts arise when a mesonephric (Wolffian) duct remnant persists in a female. They are typically located along the lateral wall of the vagina and are usually asymptomatic, but larger cysts can cause dyspareunia or urinary symptoms by compressing adjacent structures.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A persistent hymenal membrane causes an imperforate hymen obstructing the introitus, not a lateral wall cyst.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The paramesonephric ducts form the uterus, cervix, and upper vagina; their anomalies alter uterine shape rather than producing lateral vaginal wall cysts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The urogenital sinus gives rise to the lower vagina; its failure causes vaginal atresia, not a discrete lateral cyst.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The uterovaginal septum is the temporary midline partition within the uterus; failure of its resorption produces a septate uterus.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A 15-year-old girl is evaluated for primary amenorrhea and monthly episodes of pelvic pain. She has normal breast and pubic hair development. Inspection of the introitus shows only a shallow vaginal dimple, without a bulging membrane. Ultrasonography shows a normal uterus, a distended upper vagina, and normal ovaries. Failure of which of the following developmental processes most likely explains her findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Formation of the lower vagina from the urogenital sinus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Formation of the paired paramesonephric ducts in the embryo

choices.label: C
choices.text: Perforation of the hymenal membrane at the introitus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Regression of the mesonephric ducts along the vaginal wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Resorption of the midline uterovaginal septum after fusion

explanation.summary: Vaginal atresia most commonly results from failure of the lower vagina to develop from the urogenital sinus, while the paramesonephric-derived upper vagina is present.
explanation.whyCorrect: A small vaginal dimple with primary amenorrhea and a present but obstructed upper vagina is the described picture of vaginal atresia: the lower vagina never formed from the urogenital sinus, so menstrual flow has no outlet. Vaginal atresia frequently occurs as part of a broader congenital syndrome rather than in isolation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Failure of paramesonephric duct formation (MRKH syndrome) leaves no uterus and no upper vagina; this patient has both.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An imperforate hymen presents with a bulging bluish membrane at the introitus, not a shallow dimple, because the vagina behind the hymen is fully developed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A persistent mesonephric remnant forms a Gartner cyst on the lateral vaginal wall and does not prevent menstrual egress.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Failed septal resorption produces a septate uterus; it does not obstruct menstrual outflow at the vaginal level.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A 17-year-old girl is diagnosed with Mayer-von Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser syndrome after an evaluation for primary amenorrhea shows an absent uterus and upper vagina with normal ovaries. Her parents ask what caused the condition. Which of the following statements best reflects the current understanding of its etiology?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A single causative gene mutation has been definitively established

choices.label: B
choices.text: Genetic and environmental factors are both thought to contribute

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is caused by inherited mutations of the CFTR gene

choices.label: D
choices.text: It results from excess androgen exposure during fetal development

choices.label: E
choices.text: It results from persistence of a mesonephric duct remnant

explanation.summary: MRKH syndrome likely arises from a combination of genetic and environmental factors, none of which has been proven causal.
explanation.whyCorrect: Several mutations in prenatal developmental genes have been identified in patients with MRKH syndrome, but it remains unclear whether these variants directly cause the condition. Current research suggests that both genetic and environmental factors likely contribute, although the specific factors remain unknown.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Candidate variants have been found, but no single mutation has been established as directly causative.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CFTR mutations cause congenital absence of the vas deferens in males; they are not the basis of MRKH syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Excess fetal androgen exposure causes virilization of a 46,XX fetus (46,XX DSD), not agenesis of the Mullerian ducts.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A persistent mesonephric remnant produces a Gartner cyst; MRKH reflects failure of the paramesonephric ducts to form normally.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A 13-year-old girl presents with inability to urinate for the past 12 hours. She has never menstruated but has had cyclic lower abdominal pain for several months. Breast development is Tanner stage 4. Examination shows a tense, bulging bluish membrane at the vaginal introitus and a midline suprapubic mass. Which of the following best explains her urinary retention?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Compression of adjacent structures by accumulated menstrual blood

choices.label: B
choices.text: Congenital absence of the uterus and upper vagina

choices.label: C
choices.text: Failure of the lower vagina to form from the urogenital sinus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Obstruction of the urethra by a lateral vaginal wall cyst

choices.label: E
choices.text: Virilization of the external genitalia by androgen excess

explanation.summary: In severe imperforate hymen, hematocolpos and hematometra can compress adjacent structures and cause urinary retention.
explanation.whyCorrect: Menstrual blood trapped behind an unperforated hymen produces hematocolpos and hematometra, seen here as a bulging bluish membrane and a suprapubic mass. In severe cases this distended, blood-filled tract compresses adjacent structures, producing urinary retention; hymenotomy relieves the obstruction.

whyWrongByChoice.B: With MRKH syndrome there is no uterus, so menstrual blood cannot accumulate and no bulging membrane or mass develops.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vaginal atresia presents with only a small vaginal dimple at the introitus, not a bulging bluish membrane.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A Gartner cyst lies on the lateral vaginal wall and is usually asymptomatic; the finding here is a bulging hymenal membrane at the introitus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Androgen-mediated virilization alters the appearance of the external genitalia; it does not cause obstructed menstrual outflow.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A male infant born at 36 weeks' gestation has an empty left hemiscrotum on newborn examination, and the left testis is confirmed to be undescended. Which of the following is the most common location of an undescended testis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abdominal cavity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Contralateral hemiscrotum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Femoral canal

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inguinal canal

choices.label: E
choices.text: Perineum

explanation.summary: An undescended testis typically lies along the normal pathway of descent, most commonly within the inguinal canal.
explanation.whyCorrect: In cryptorchidism the testis fails to complete its descent into the scrotum and is typically found along the normal pathway of descent. The most common location is the inguinal canal. Cryptorchidism is associated with prematurity because descent occurs late in fetal development.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Descent can arrest within the abdomen, but this is not the most common site; the inguinal canal is.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cryptorchidism is failure of descent along the normal pathway, not migration of the testis to the opposite hemiscrotum.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The femoral canal is not part of the normal pathway of testicular descent described for cryptorchidism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The perineum is not along the normal route of descent from abdomen to scrotum.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A boy born at 34 weeks' gestation is noted at his newborn examination to have an empty right hemiscrotum, with a smooth mass palpable in the right inguinal region. He is otherwise healthy. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Immediate orchiectomy of the undescended right testis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Karyotype analysis for a suspected disorder of sexual development

choices.label: C
choices.text: Observation with re-examination during the first year of life

choices.label: D
choices.text: Orchiopexy before hospital discharge in the newborn period

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ultrasound-guided needle aspiration of the inguinal mass

explanation.summary: Most undescended testes descend spontaneously within the first year of life; surgery is reserved for those that have not descended by one year.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cryptorchidism is associated with prematurity because testicular descent occurs late in fetal development. In many infants the testis descends spontaneously within the first year, so careful observation is the appropriate initial approach. If descent has not occurred by one year, orchiopexy is recommended to reduce the risks of infertility and testicular germ cell tumors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Removal of the testis is not the described management; orchiopexy repositions the testis if spontaneous descent fails.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Isolated cryptorchidism in a premature infant reflects incomplete late-fetal descent and does not itself indicate a DSD workup.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Surgical correction is recommended only if the testis has not descended by one year of age, not in the newborn period.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The inguinal mass is the undescended testis lying along its pathway of descent, not a fluid collection to aspirate.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: The parents of a 14-month-old boy with a persistently undescended testis in the inguinal canal are counseled about the risks of leaving the condition uncorrected before scheduled orchiopexy. Which of the following best explains the increased risk of testicular germ cell tumors in this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chronic exposure of the undescended testis to peritoneal fluid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disrupted germ cell differentiation leaving immature germ cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Loss of Leydig cell testosterone production in the testis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mechanical compression of the testis within the narrow inguinal canal

choices.label: E
choices.text: Recurrent torsion of the malpositioned inguinal testis

explanation.summary: Higher temperatures outside the scrotum disrupt germ cell differentiation, leaving immature germ cells prone to malignant transformation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Testes that remain in the abdomen or inguinal canal are exposed to temperatures higher than the scrotum. This disrupts normal germ cell differentiation, leaving immature germ cells that are more prone to malignant transformation, which is why orchiopexy is recommended if descent has not occurred by one year.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Peritoneal fluid tracking into the scrotum is the mechanism of a communicating hydrocele, not of tumor formation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The lecture attributes the malignancy risk to temperature-disrupted germ cell differentiation, not to loss of hormone production.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mechanical compression is not the described mechanism; the key factor is the higher temperature outside the scrotum.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Torsion is not described as the link between cryptorchidism and germ cell tumors.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A boy born at 33 weeks' gestation has painless swelling of the right hemiscrotum. Ultrasonography shows an anechoic fluid collection surrounding the right testis, and the processus vaginalis is confirmed to be closed. Which of the following best describes this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abdominal contents herniating through a widely patent processus vaginalis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Arrest of the testis along its normal pathway of descent

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fluid trapped in the tunica vaginalis behind a closed processus vaginalis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fluid within a persistent remnant of the mesonephric duct

choices.label: E
choices.text: Peritoneal fluid entering the scrotum through a patent processus vaginalis

explanation.summary: A noncommunicating hydrocele occurs when the processus vaginalis has closed but fluid remains trapped within the tunica vaginalis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Congenital hydroceles are classified by whether the processus vaginalis remains open. Here the processus vaginalis is closed, so this is a noncommunicating (acquired) hydrocele, in which fluid is trapped within the tunica vaginalis. This type is common in newborns, especially premature infants, and also occurs in adults.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Herniation of abdominal contents describes an indirect inguinal hernia, a risk of a widely patent processus vaginalis, not this closed-sac fluid collection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The testis in this infant is descended and surrounded by fluid; arrested descent is cryptorchidism with an empty scrotum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mesonephric duct remnants persist as Gartner cysts in females; they are not the source of scrotal fluid here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ongoing entry of peritoneal fluid defines a communicating hydrocele, which requires an incompletely closed processus vaginalis.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy has right scrotal swelling that has been present since infancy. Evaluation confirms a communicating hydrocele with an incompletely closed processus vaginalis. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Continued observation until adolescence

choices.label: B
choices.text: Needle aspiration of the scrotal fluid

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oral antibiotic therapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Orchiopexy of the right testis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surgical repair of the hydrocele

explanation.summary: A communicating hydrocele that persists beyond early childhood should be surgically repaired.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most communicating hydroceles resolve spontaneously during the first year of life, but those that persist beyond early childhood are less likely to resolve and surgical repair is usually recommended. A widely patent processus vaginalis also increases the risk of an indirect inguinal hernia, adding to the rationale for repair.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The window for expected spontaneous resolution is the first year of life; at age 4 continued observation leaves a persistent peritoneal connection and hernia risk.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aspiration does not close the patent processus vaginalis, which is the underlying defect allowing peritoneal fluid into the tunica vaginalis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The swelling is peritoneal fluid within the tunica vaginalis, not an infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Orchiopexy treats cryptorchidism; this boy's testis is descended.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: During normal male development, an embryonic structure accompanies the testis during its descent into the scrotum and is then obliterated late in development, leaving the tunica vaginalis as a closed sac around the testis. This structure is an outpouching of which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Genital tubercle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mesonephric duct

choices.label: C
choices.text: Paramesonephric duct

choices.label: D
choices.text: Peritoneum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Urogenital sinus

explanation.summary: The processus vaginalis is an embryonic outpouching of peritoneum that accompanies the descending testis and is normally obliterated.
explanation.whyCorrect: The processus vaginalis is an outpouching of peritoneum that travels with the testis during descent. Its normal obliteration leaves the tunica vaginalis as a closed serous sac around the testis; incomplete closure allows peritoneal fluid into the sac, producing a communicating hydrocele.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The genital tubercle contributes to external genital development; its abnormal dorsal position causes epispadias.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The mesonephric duct persists abnormally in females as a Gartner cyst; it does not form the processus vaginalis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The paramesonephric ducts form the uterus, cervix, and upper vagina and are unrelated to the coverings of the testis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The urogenital sinus contributes to the lower vagina in females; it is not the origin of the processus vaginalis.

questions.topicName: Congenital Disorders of the Reproductive Systems

questions.stem: A newborn boy has a urethral opening located on the ventral surface of the penis at the junction of the penis and scrotum, with a hooded dorsal foreskin. Which of the following best classifies this anomaly?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Distal hypospadias

choices.label: B
choices.text: Epispadias

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glanular hypospadias

choices.label: D
choices.text: Proximal hypospadias

choices.label: E
